MAJAZ:v1p56/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p56/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p56/r1.claim: ويزكيهم means purify them; زكية in the other verse means purified.

ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r11.claim: The requested messenger will recite God's signs, teach scripture and wisdom, and purify the people; wisdom means mastery in knowledge and action, accuracy in speech and deed, a topic developed at 2:269.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r11.anchor: Asl-ı “hikmet”, ilm ü amelde itkan, ta‘bîr-i âharla kavl ü fiilde isabet demektir

ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r12.claim: The messenger is Muhammad, since no other prophet from Ishmael's descendants is agreed upon; his hadith identifies him as Abraham's prayer, Jesus' good news, and his mother's vision.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r12.anchor: Bu resulden murad da Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ Muhammed Mustafâ sallâllahu aleyhi ve sellem olduğu âşikârdır

ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r13.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r13.claim: The Prophet says he is the prayer of his father Abraham, the glad tidings of his brother Jesus, and his mother's vision.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r13.anchor: أَنَا دَعْوَةُ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَبُشْرَى أخي عِيسَى وَرُؤْيَا أُمِّي

ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r14.claim: As thanks for Abraham's prayer, Muhammad's community was taught to invoke blessings on Muhammad and his family as God blessed Abraham and his family; these verses clarify the meaning and basis of that comparison.
ELMALILI:2:124-133#2/r14.anchor: bu duasına şükrâne olmak üzeredir ki ümmet-i Muhammed’e de namazlarda

SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r1.claim: منهم is accusative as an adjective of رسولا, attached to an omitted phrase meaning a messenger belonging to them.
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r1.anchor: في محل نصب لأنه صفة لرسولا فيتعلق بمحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r2.claim: يتلو may be accusative as a second adjective of رسولا; al-Samīn calls this the best order.
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r2.anchor: صفة ثانية لرسولا، وجاء هذا على الترتيب الأحسن

SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r3.claim: Alternatively, يتلو is circumstantial to رسولا, made specific through the adjective.
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r3.anchor: في محل نصب على الحال من " رسولا " لأنه لما وصف تخصص

SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r4.claim: A third parse makes يتلو circumstantial to the pronoun in منهم, governed by the implied existential verb.
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r4.anchor: حال من الضمير في " منهم " والعامل فيها الاستقرار

SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r5.claim: العزيز comes first as an attribute of essence, while الحكيم follows as an attribute of action.
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r5.anchor: وتقدم قوله " العزيز " لأنها صفة ذات وتأخر " الحكيم " لأنها صفة فعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r6.claim: عز varies by vowel: with ḍamma it means prevail, as in وعزني في الخطاب; with fatḥa strength, and with kasra preciousness and rarity.
SAMIN-DURR:2:129/r6.anchor: فالمضموم بمعنى غلب ومنه: وعزني في الخطاب

ASAD-NOTES:2:129#n106/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:129#n106/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:129#n106/r1.claim: Asad notes that the phrase translated “from among them” literally means “within them.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r7.claim: Abraham prayed for an Ishmaelite messenger with the same tasks named in 62:2: reciting revelation, teaching law and wisdom, and purifying the people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r7.anchor: Abraham (sws) had prayed to God to send forth a prophet among the Ishmaelites having exactly these attributes.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r8.claim: Muhammad manifests both God’s attributes and Abraham’s prayer, and combines several distinct attributes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p316/r8.anchor: just as Muḥammad (sws) is a manifestation of the attributes of God, he is also a manifestation of the prayer of Abraham (sws)

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p76/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p76/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p76/r4.claim: In several forms, including ويعلمهم الكتاب, Abū ʿAmr lightly rounds or lowers the vowel before hāʾ rather than fully articulating it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p76/r4.anchor: من ذلك ما حدثني عبيد الله بن علي الهاشمي عن نصر بن علي عن أبيه عنه أنه كان يقرأ ويعلمهم الكتاب

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p82/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p82/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p82/r1.claim: A deleted vowel can remain grammatically intended, just as deleted yāʾ or wāw in other forms does not erase the underlying vowel’s status.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p82/r1.anchor: وكان حذفها بمنزلة إثباتها في الجواز كما كانت الحركة فيما ذكرنا كذلك

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p82/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p82/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p82/r2.claim: Vowels can be fully articulated or shortened by ikhtilās, but only ḍamma and kasra are shortened this way; fatḥa is not.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p82/r2.anchor: وهذا الاختلاس والتخفيف إنما يكون في الضمة والكسرة، فأما الفتحة فليس فيها إلا الإشباع

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p82/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p82/r3.speaker: سيبويه
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p82/r3.claim: Sībawayh treats the forms including ويعلمهم الكتاب as shortened vowels, not sukūn; weak, faint pronunciation explains why some transmitters mistook ikhtilās for silence.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r1.claim: The author sides with the Basrans: constructions of this kind contain an intended, elided قول; the Kufans instead take the wording as carrying the sense of speech without an implicit verb.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r1.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: في هذا دليل على صحة ما يذهب إليه أصحابنا من أن القول مراد مقدر

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's cited reading makes the normally presumed speech verb overt, which the author treats as decisive evidence for the Basran analysis.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r2.anchor: وقد رأيت إلى قراءة ابن مسعود كيف ظهر فيها ما نقدره من القول

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r3.claim: The poem أخبرانا إنا رأينا can mean قالا إنا under the Basran ellipsis analysis; the Kufan account instead treats أخبرانا as already meaning قالا لنا. Calling Anter and the angels' greeting also omit القول.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r3.anchor: فهو عندنا نحن على: قالا: إنا رأينا، وعلى قولهم لا إضمار قول هناك؛

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r4.speaker: عباس ناقلا عن أبي عمرو
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr describes Hijazi gemination in يعلمهم ويلعنهم, against the light forms attributed to Tamim.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r4.anchor: قال عباس: سألت أبا عمرو عن {ويعلمهم الكتاب} فقال: أهل الحجاز يقولون:

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r5.claim: Gemination needs no defense; lightening is explained by the burden of successive vowels, relieved by dropping a case vowel, as in Abū ʿAmr's بارئكم and Abū Zayd's يكتبون.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r5.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: أما التثقيل فلا سؤال عنه ولا فيه؛ لأنه استيفاء واجب الإعراب؛ لكن من حذف فعنه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r6.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r6.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās's objection to the grammatical book is really directed at the Arabs whose usage it records; the cited form is also required by poetic meter.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p108/r6.anchor: فإنما هو على العرب لا على صاحب الكتاب؛ لأنه حكاه كما سمعه، ولا يمكن في الوزن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r3.claim: After prayers for Mecca’s security, its people’s provision, and a submissive community from Abraham’s descendants, the prayer concludes by asking for Muḥammad’s mission, which secures their worldly and otherworldly happiness through safety, abundance, and guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r3.anchor: لما دعا ربه بالأمن لمكة، وبالرزق لأهلها، وبأن يجعل من ذريته أمة مسلمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r4.claim: Baʿth here means sending or commissioning as a messenger, as in the earlier explanation of the root in the Qurʾān.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r4.anchor: وقد تقدم معنى البعث في قوله: ثم بعثناكم، والمراد هنا: الإرسال إليهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r5.claim: The pronoun in fīhim may refer to Abraham’s descendants, the submissive community, or the people of Mecca; the last is supported by the description of a messenger among the unlettered. The messenger is undisputedly Muḥammad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r5.anchor: والضمير في فيهم يحتمل أن يعود على الذرية، ويحتمل أن يعود على أمة مسلمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r6.speaker: محمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r6.claim: A sound report has Muḥammad say, ‘I am the invocation of my father Abraham’; Abū Ḥayyān adds that God sent no one to Mecca and its surroundings except him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r6.anchor:
ولا خلاف أنه رسول الله محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وصح عنه
أنه قال: «أنا دعوة أبي إبراهيم»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r7.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r7.claim: Ubay reads وابعث فيهم في آخرهم, specifying their latter members.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبي: وابعث فيهم في آخرهم، قال ابن عباس:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says all prophets were from the Children of Israel except ten, whom he names: Noah, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Shuʿayb, Lūṭ, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, and Muḥammad (the excerpt’s count and list are as reported).
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كل الأنبياء من بني إسرائيل إلا عشرة: نوح، وهود، وصالح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r9.claim: Minhum is an adjective of rasūlan: the messenger is from the people, not outsiders, so they know his face, lineage, upbringing, truthfulness, and trustworthiness; an insider is more compassionate and more readily accepted and honored.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625/r9.anchor: ومنهم في موضع الصفة لرسولا، أي كائنا منهم لا من غيرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r1.claim: Abraham’s prayer has been answered; the requested messenger appears at the end of time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r1.anchor: قد استجيب لك، وهو في آخر الزمان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r2.claim: The recitation clause may be an adjective describing messenger, or a circumstantial clause since he is already described as one of them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r2.anchor: جملة في موضع الصفة لرسولا. وقيل: في موضع الحال منه، لأنه قد وصف بقوله منهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r3.claim: God fulfilled Abraham’s request in its fullest terms: Muhammad recited God’s signs and received the Quran, the greatest miracle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r3.anchor: ووصف إبراهيم الرسول بأنه يكون يتلو عليهم آيات الله، أي يقرؤها، فكان كذلك، وأوتي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن، وهو أعظم المعجزات.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r4.claim: The signs here are the Quran; another explanation takes them as accounts of past and future events through the Resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r4.anchor: والآيات هنا آيات القرآن. وقيل: خبر من مضى، وخبر من يأتي إلى يوم القيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r5.speaker: الفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r5.claim: Al-Faḍl explains the recitation as making their religion clear to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r5.anchor: وقال الفضل: معناه يبين لهم دينهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r6.claim: The Book is the Quran, and teaching it means helping them understand and conveying its meanings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r6.anchor: ويعلمهم الكتاب: هو القرآن، والمعنى: أنه يفهمهم ويلقي إليهم معانيه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r7.claim: Recitation comes before teaching because listeners first hear the Quran, then learn its meanings and reflect on them; teaching is attributed to the Messenger as communicator and facilitator.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r7.anchor: وكان ترتيب التعليم بعد التلاوة، لأنه أول ما يقرع السمع هو التلاوة والتلفظ بالقرآن، ثم بعد ذلك تتعلم معانيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r8.claim: Teaching can mean producing understanding and knowledge in a learner, or merely supplying the means to knowledge; this explains why learning may or may not follow.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r8.anchor: والتعليم يكون بمعنى التفهيم وحصول العلم للمتعلم، ويكون بمعنى إلقاء أسباب العلم، ولا يحصل به العلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the Messenger recites and conveys revelations proving God’s oneness and the prophets’ truth; the Book is the Quran, and wisdom is the Sharia and exposition of rulings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري: يتلو عليهم آياتك: يقرأ عليهم، ويبلغهم ما يوحي إليه من دلائل وحدانيتك وصدق أنبيائك، ويعلمهم الكتاب القرآن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r10.claim: Qatadah identifies wisdom with the Sunnah and the Prophet’s explanation of the laws.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة: الحكمة: السنة، وبيان النبي: الشرائع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r11.speaker: مالك وأبو رزين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r11.claim: Malik and Abu Razin take wisdom as religious understanding and an innate understanding or light from God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r11.anchor: وقال مالك وأبو رزين: الحكمة، الفقه في الدين، والفهم الذي هو سجية ونور من الله تعالى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r12.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r12.claim: Mujahid defines wisdom as understanding the Quran.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r13.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r13.claim: Muqatil says wisdom is knowledge joined to practice; a person is not wise without both.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r13.anchor: وقال مقاتل: العلم والعمل به لا يكون الرجل حكيما حتى يجمعهما.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r14.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r14.claim: One reported definition of wisdom is judgment and adjudication.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r14.anchor: وقيل: الحكم والقضاء. وقيل: ما لا يعلم إلا من جهة الرسول.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r15.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r15.claim: Another definition is whatever can only be known through the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r15.anchor: وقيل: الحكم والقضاء. وقيل: ما لا يعلم إلا من جهة الرسول.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r16.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r16.claim: Ibn Zayd calls any word that admonishes, urges virtue, or forbids vice wisdom.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r16.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: كل كلمة وعظتك، أو دعتك إلى مكرمة، أو نهتك عن قبيح فهي حكمة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r17.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r17.claim: Some say wisdom here is the Book, repeated for emphasis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r17.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الحكمة هنا الكتاب، وكررها توكيدا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r18.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن يعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r18.claim: Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn Yaʿqub defines wisdom as every sound statement that produces sound action.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p625#2/r18.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر محمد بن يعقوب: كل صواب من القول ورث فعلا صحيحا فهو حكمة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r1.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r1.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh depicts wisdom as a divine force sent into knowers’ hearts to refresh them from worldly heat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r1.anchor: الحكمة جند من جنود الله، يرسلها الله إلى قلوب العارفين حتى يروح عنها وهج الدنيا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r2.claim: One reported definition of wisdom is putting things in their proper places.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r2.anchor: وقيل: هي وضع الأشياء مواضعها. وقيل: كل قول وجب فعله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r3.claim: Another definition is every saying whose enactment is obligatory.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r3.anchor: وقيل: هي وضع الأشياء مواضعها. وقيل: كل قول وجب فعله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r4.claim: The definitions converge on two senses, Quran and Sunnah: the Sunnah explains the Book’s ambiguities and reveals the aspects of its rulings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r4.anchor: وهذه الأقوال في الحكمة كلها متقاربة، ويجمع هذه الأقوال قولان: أحدهما، القرآن والآخر السنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r5.claim: Reciting the signs means clearly articulating the Quran’s words and showing how it is properly recited, including its delivery and pauses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r5.anchor: أي يفصح لهم عن ألفاظه ويوقفهم بقراءته على كيفية تلاوته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r6.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r6.claim: The Prophet told Ubayy that God had commanded him to recite the Quran to him, so Ubayy could learn its proper performance and divisions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r6.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي: «إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك القرآن»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r7.claim: Teaching the Book means explaining its rulings and contents: lawful and forbidden matters, duties, recommendations, exhortations, parables, promises, threats, resurrection, judgment, and afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r7.anchor: وفي قوله: ويعلمهم الكتاب، أي يبين لهم وجوه أحكامه: حلاله وحرامه، ومفروضه، ومسنونه، ومواعظه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r8.claim: Wisdom is the Sunnah, which clarifies Quranic generalities and ambiguities, supplies details the Quran omits, and establishes rulings not contained in it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r8.anchor: وفي قوله: والحكمة، أي السنة تبين ما في الكتاب من المجمل، وتوضح ما انبهم من المشكل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r9.claim: The Messenger purifies people inwardly from shirk and doubt, and outwardly through duties that cleanse sins and bring blessings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r9.anchor: ويزكيهم باطنا من أرجاس الشرك وأنجاس الشك، وظاهرا بالتكاليف التي تمحص الآثام وتوصل الإنعام.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains purification as obedience and sincerity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: التزكية: الطاعة والإخلاص.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r11.claim: Ibn Jurayj says purification means cleansing people of shirk.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r11.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: يطهرهم من الشرك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r12.claim: One view takes the phrase to mean collecting zakat from them, which purifies them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r12.anchor: وقيل: يأخذ منهم الزكاة التي تكون سببا لطهرتهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r13.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r13.claim: Another view takes it as inviting them to what will make them pure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r13.anchor: وقيل: يدعوا إلى ما يصيرون به أزكياء. وقيل: يشهد لهم بالتزكية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r14.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r14.claim: A further view says the Messenger testifies to their uprightness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r14.anchor: وقيل: يشهد لهم بالتزكية من تزكية العدول، ومعنى الزكاة لا تخرج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r15.claim: The word zakat always stays within the meanings of purification or growth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r15.anchor: ومعنى الزكاة لا تخرج عن التطهير أو التنمية.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r16.claim: Al-ʿAziz can mean the dominant or the unassailable, whom no one can reach.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r16.anchor: العزيز: الغالب، أو المنيع الذي لا يرام، قاله المفضل بن سلمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r17.speaker: ابن كيسان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r17.claim: Ibn Kaysan defines al-ʿAziz as the one whom nothing can defeat or frustrate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r17.anchor: أو الذي لا يعجزه شيء، قاله ابن كيسان، أو الذي لا مثل له، قاله ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas defines al-ʿAziz as the one without equal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r18.anchor: أو الذي لا يعجزه شيء، قاله ابن كيسان، أو الذي لا مثل له، قاله ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r19.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r19.claim: Al-Kalbi defines al-ʿAziz as the avenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r19.anchor: أو المنتقم، قاله الكلبي، أو القوي، ومنه فعزنا بثالث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r20.claim: Al-ʿAziz can also mean the strong; the cited wording says God strengthened them with a third.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r20.anchor: أو المنتقم، قاله الكلبي، أو القوي، ومنه فعزنا بثالث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r21.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r21.claim: Al-ʿAziz can mean the one who grants honor, as in the Quranic phrase about honoring whom God wills.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r21.anchor: أو المعز ومنه: وتعز من تشاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r22.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r22.claim: The commentary has already explained al-Hakim in the story of the angels and Adam, in the phrase ending “the All-knowing, the Wise.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r22.anchor: قد تقدم تفسير الحكيم في قصة الملائكة وآدم في قوله: إلا ما علمتنا إنك أنت العليم الحكيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r23.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r23.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r23.claim: The parsing possibilities for anta here are the same as those discussed earlier for anta al-Samiʿ al-ʿAlim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r23.anchor: وأنت: يجوز فيها ما جاز في أنت السميع العليم قبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r24.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r24.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r24.claim: Might and wisdom suit the preceding request: only such a God can send the Messenger described, placing prophecy in His noblest creature; al-ʿAziz precedes al-Hakim as an essential attribute before an attribute of action, and al-Hakim fits the verse endings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p626/r24.anchor: وهاتان الصفتان متناسبتان لما قبلهما، لأن إرسال رسول متصف بالأوصاف التي سألها إبراهيم لا تصدر إلا عمن اتصف بالعزة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r1.claim: “Among them” means in the Muslim community.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r1.anchor: أي أرسل في الأمة المسلمة وقيل : في الذرية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r2.claim: An alternative takes “among them” to mean among Abraham’s descendants.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r2.anchor: أي أرسل في الأمة المسلمة وقيل : في الذرية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r3.claim: Referring the pronoun to the people of Mecca is far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r3.anchor: وعود الضمير إلى أهل مكة بعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r4.claim: A messenger from their own people would be compassionate, honored, and readily believed because they knew his origins, truthfulness, and trustworthiness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r4.anchor: ووصفه بذلك ليكون أشفق عليهم ويكونوا أعز به واشرف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r5.claim: Only Muhammad descended from both Abraham and Ishmael; the other Israelite prophets descended from Abraham, not from both, so Muhammad fulfilled their joint prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r5.anchor: ولم يبعث من ذرية كليهما سوى محمد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r6.claim: The Prophet said he was Abraham’s prayer, Jesus’s glad tidings, and the vision his mother saw at his birth; al-Alusi cites Ahmad and Sharh al-Sunna without grading it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r6.anchor: عن العرباض عن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أنه قال : سأخبركم بأول أمري أنا دعوة إبراهيم وبشارة عيسى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r7.claim: “Abraham’s prayer” may mean its outcome, its recipient, or the very prayer itself by emphatic expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r7.anchor: وأراد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إثر دعوته أو مدعوه أو عين دعوته على المبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r8.claim: Since Ishmael shared the supplication, Muhammad was Ishmael’s prayer too; Abraham is named for nobility and his foundational role in the supplication.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r8.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم دعوة إسماعيل أيضا إلا أنه خص إبراهيم لشرافته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r9.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the claim that naming only Abraham in the hadith proves Ishmael’s prayer was not answered.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r9.anchor: وهم من قال : إن الإقتصار في الحديث على إبراهيم يدل على أن المجاب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r10.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r10.claim: Ubayy read “and raise among them, among their last ones, a messenger,” supporting identification with Muhammad.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( وأبعث فيهم في آخرهم رسولا ) وهذا يويد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r11.claim: The signs are revealed proofs of divine oneness, prophethood, and related truths, recited by the messenger.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r11.anchor: من العلامات الدالة على التوحيد والنبوة وغيرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r12.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r12.claim: Another interpretation takes the signs as reports of past and future events through the Day of Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r12.anchor: وقيل : خبر من مضى ومن يأتي إلى يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r13.claim: The recitation clause is either an adjective of “messenger” or a circumstantial clause referring to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r13.anchor: والجملة صفة ( رسولا ) وقيل : في موضع الحال منه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r14.claim: Teaching the Book means explaining its wording and mode of recitation, and acquainting them with its realities and secrets.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r14.anchor: بأن يفهمهم ألفاظه ويبين لهم كيفية أدائه ويوقفهم على حقائقه وأسراره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r15.claim: The prayer’s apparent aim is a scripture-bearing messenger leading people from ignorance to knowledge; the Qur’an fulfills it, though its being specifically requested is not explicit.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r15.anchor: أن يكون الرسول صاحب كتاب يخرجهم من ظلمة الجهل إلى نور العلم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r16.claim: One proposed sense of wisdom is putting things in their proper places.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r17.claim: Another proposed sense is what removes the heart’s ardent attachment to worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r17.anchor: ما يزيل من القلوب وهج حب الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r18.claim: Wisdom is also explained as religious jurisprudence or the Sunna that clarifies the Book.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r18.anchor: أو الفقه في الدين أو السنة المبينة للكتاب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r19.claim: Some take wisdom as the Book itself, repeated for emphasis and care.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r19.anchor: وكرر للتأكيد إعتناء بشأنه وقد يقال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r20.claim: Wisdom may mean the Book’s embedded truths and subtleties, with teaching its wording and wisdom its inner contents.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r20.anchor: المراد بها حقائق الكتاب ودقائقه وسائر ما أودع فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r21.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r21.claim: Some define wisdom as knowledge and rulings by which souls are perfected theoretically and practically.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r21.anchor: وفسرها بعضهم بما تكمل به النفوس من المعارف والأحكام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r22.claim: Al-Alusi challenges the claim that some soul-perfecting matters lie outside the Qur’an after declarations that it omits nothing and explains everything; he allows a distinction for the scripture requested before the answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r22.anchor: ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r23.claim: Purification means cleansing them of idolatry, doubt, and sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r23.anchor: أي يطهرهم من أرجاس الشرك وأنجاس الشك وقاذورات المعاصي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r24.claim: Teaching adorns the soul and purification empties it of defilement; precedence of adornment is attributed to its nobility.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r24.anchor: كما أن التعليم إشارة إلى التحلية ولعل تقديم الثاني على الأول لشرافته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r25.claim: Taking this as collecting alms from them or attesting to their purity and uprightness is far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r25.anchor: والقول بأن المراد يأخذ منهم الزكاة التي هي سبب لطهرتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r26.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r26.claim: “Mighty, Wise” means overpowering and effecting whatever He wills; God can single someone out for this mission without an external selector.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r26.anchor: أي الغالب المحكم لما يريد فلك أن تخصص واحدا منهم بالرسالة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r27.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r27.claim: Al-Alusi finds distant Ibn Abbas’s gloss of “Mighty” as peerless, al-Kalbi’s as avenger, and “Wise” as simply knowing.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p386/r27.anchor: وحمل ( العزيز ) هنا على من لا مثل له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r1.claim: Among them refers to the Muslim community descended from Abraham and Ishmael; another view says it means the people of Mecca.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r1.anchor: أي في الأمة المسلمة من ذرية إبراهيم وإسماعيل وقيل: من أهل مكة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r2.claim: The messenger intended is Muhammad, sent from among them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r2.anchor: {رسولا منهم} أي مرسلا منهم أراد به محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r3.speaker: العرباض بن سارية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r3.claim: Al-Irbad ibn Sariya reports the Prophet said he was recorded as the seal of prophets while Adam was still in clay, and named Abraham's prayer, Jesus' good news, and his mother's vision of light illuminating Syria's palaces as signs of his mission.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r3.anchor: عن العرباض بن سارية عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إني عند الله مكتوب خاتم النبيين،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r4.claim: The Prophet's reference to Abraham's prayer is this request for a messenger among the descendants of Ishmael.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r4.anchor: وأراد بدعوة إبراهيم هذا فإنه دعا أن يبعث في بني إسماعيل رسولا منهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says all prophets were Israelites except ten: Noah, Hud, Salih, Shuayb, Lot, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and Muhammad.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p151#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كل الأنبياء من بني إسرائيل إلا عشرة: نوح وهود وصالح وشعيب ولوط وإبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب ومحمد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r1.claim: Yatlu means to recite; God's signs here are His book, the Quran. An ayah is connected speech up to a break, or a group of letters; the idiom can mean a gathered group.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r1.anchor: {يتلو} يقرأ {عليهم آياتك} كتابك يعني القرآن والآية من القرآن كلام متصل إلى انقطاعه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r3.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r3.claim: Mujahid explains wisdom as understanding the Quran.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r4.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r4.claim: Muqatil explains wisdom as the Quran's exhortations and its rulings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: مواعظ القرآن وما فيه من الأحكام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba says wisdom is knowledge joined with action; a person is not wise until possessing both.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r5.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة: هي العلم والعمل، ولا يكون الرجل حكيما حتى يجمعهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r6.claim: Other explanations of wisdom are the Sunna, rulings and judgment, or jurisprudence.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r6.anchor: وقيل: هي السنة، وقيل: هي الأحكام والقضاء وقيل: الحكمة الفقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r7.speaker: أبو بكر بن دريد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r7.claim: Ibn Durayd calls any saying that admonishes, urges virtue, or forbids wrongdoing wisdom.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r7.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن دريد: كل كلمة وعظتك أو دعتك إلى مكرمة أو نهتك عن قبيح فهي حكمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r8.claim: Yuzakkihim means purify them from polytheism and sins; another view takes it as collecting their alms.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r8.anchor: {ويزكيهم} أي يطهرهم من الشرك والذنوب، وقيل: يأخذ الزكاة من أموالهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r9.speaker: ابن كيسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r9.claim: Ibn Kaysan derives the word from attesting to their uprightness on Judgment Day when they testify that the prophets conveyed their message.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r9.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: يشهد لهم يوم القيامة بالعدالة إذا شهدوا للأنبياء بالبلاغ من التزكية، وهي التعديل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas explains al-Aziz as the One without equal.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: العزيز الذي لا يوجد مثله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r11.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r11.claim: Al-Kalbi explains it as the Avenger, citing the description of God as mighty and possessing retribution.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r11.anchor: وقال الكلبي: المنتقم بيانه قوله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r12.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r12.claim: Other explanations are the invulnerable One, whom hands cannot reach, and the Strong One; عز means strength, as in We strengthened with a third.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r12.anchor: وقيل: المنيع الذي لا تناله الأيدي ولا يصل إليه شيء وقيل: القوي، والعزة القوة قال الله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r13.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r13.claim: Another explanation is the Overpowering One; the expression عزني في الخطاب means he overcame me in speech, and the proverb says the victor takes the spoils.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p152/r13.anchor: وقيل: الغالب قال الله تعالى إخبارا

BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r2.claim: The prayer asks for a messenger from among the Muslim community descended from Abraham and Ishmael; being sent among them does not itself entail being one of them.
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r2.anchor: أي : من أنفسهم فإن البعث فيهم لا يستلزم البعث منهم

BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r3.claim: Muhammad is the only prophet from Abraham and Ishmael’s descendants, and he is the one who answers their prayer.
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r3.anchor: ولم يبعث من ذريتهما غير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهو الذي أجيب به دعوتهما

BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r4.speaker: راوٍ غير مسمى
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r4.claim: A report says Abraham was told his prayer would be answered at the end of time.
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r4.anchor: روي أنه قيل له قد استجيب لك وهو في آخر الزمان

BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r5.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r5.claim: The Prophet says he was designated the Seal of Prophets while Adam was still in clay, and names Abraham’s prayer, Jesus’ good news, and his mother’s vision of light illuminating Syrian palaces as the beginnings of his mission.
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث "إني عند الله مكتوب خاتم النبيين وأن آدم لمجدل في طينته

BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r6.claim: Abraham’s specific invocation was the request that God send a messenger among the Israelites.
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r6.anchor: وأراد بدعوة إبراهيم هذا فإنه دعا الله أن يبعث في بني إسرائيل رسولا منهم

BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r7.claim: The messenger recites and conveys revelations that establish monotheism and prophethood.
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r7.anchor: يقرأ عليهم ويبلغهم ما يوحى إليه من دلائل التوحيد والنبوة

BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r8.claim: Teaching develops their theoretical faculty: the Book is the Qur’an, and wisdom is true knowledge and the religious rulings that perfect the soul.
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r8.anchor: وما يكمل به نفوسهم من المعارف الحقة والأحكام الشرعية

BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r9.speaker: ابن دريد
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r9.claim: Ibn Durayd defines wisdom as any saying that admonishes, directs someone toward virtue, or forbids a wrong.
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r9.anchor: قال ابن دريد : كل كلمة وعظتك أو دعتك إلى مكرمة أو نهتك عن قبيح فهي حكمة

BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r10.claim: Purification develops the practical faculty by cleansing people of polytheism and sins, whether through neglecting duties or committing wrongs.
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r10.anchor: من دنس الشرك وفنون المعاصي سواء كانت بترك الواجبات أو بفعل المنكرات

BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r11.claim: Abraham closes with praise: God is mighty, prevailing over what He wills, and wise, acting only as wisdom and benefit require; all else is inherently weak and ignorant.
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r11.anchor: الذي يقهر ويغلب على ما يريد

BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r12.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r12.claim: Al-Ghazali begins defining the Divine Name al-ʿAziz as one who is eminent and rare, urgently needed, and difficult to reach.
BURSEVI:v1p187#3/r12.anchor: قال الإمام الغزالي قدس سره في "شرح الأسماء الحسنى" العزيز : هو الخطير الذي يقل وجود مثله

BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r1.claim: Sending messengers serves a wise benefit: they order outward life, illuminate the inward, and organize the world; their heirs, the perfected saints, inherit a special share in purification.
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r1.anchor: لأن عمارة الظاهر وإنارة الباطن ونظام العالم بهم لا بغيرهم ولورثتهم من الأولياء الكاملين حظ أوفى

BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r2.claim: A servant needs a guide and spiritual mentor to reach the goal; without a shaykh, Satan becomes his shaykh.
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r2.anchor: فلا بد للعبد من دليل ومرشد يهتدي به إلى مقصوده ومن لم يكن له شيخ فشيخه الشيطان

BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r3.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r3.claim: Hafiz’s Persian verse cautions against entering the path of love without a guide, since self-directed striving failed him despite great effort.
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r3.anchor: قال الحافظ : بكوى عشق منه بي دليل رآه قدم كه من بخويش نمودم صد اهتمام ونشد

BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r4.claim: A perfected guide, with God’s permission, purifies the seeker from attention to anything besides God and recites signs within the self and in the horizons, leading to certainty, spiritual joy, and the company of the truthful.
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r4.anchor: والمرشد الكامل يزكي نفس السالك بإذن الله ويطهرها من دنس الالتفات إلى ما سوى الله ويتلو عليه الآيات الأنفسية والآفاقية

BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r5.claim: The phrase “and purifies them” points to spiritual wayfaring and guiding; the passage ends with a prayer for protection from obstacles on the path to God.
BURSEVI:v1p188#2/r5.anchor: يشير إلى السلوك والتسليك فاحفظ هذا وليكن على ذكر منك اللهم احفظنا من الموانع في طريق الوصول إليك

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129/r14.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129/r14.claim: The Prophet said he was the answered prayer of Abraham, the glad tidings of Jesus, and his mother’s vision.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129/r14.anchor: " أنا دعوة إبراهيم، وبشرى عيسى، ورؤيا أمي "

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129/r15.claim: The requested messenger is from the submitted community; Muhammad was the only descendant of Abraham and Ishmael sent as such, answering their prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129/r15.anchor: في الأمة المسلمة { رسولامنهم } ولم يبعث من ذريتهما غير محمد

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r1.claim: The messenger recites and conveys the signs God reveals, including proofs of divine unity and prophethood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r1.anchor: يقرأ عليهم ويبلغهم ما توحي إليه من دلائل التوحيد والنبوة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r2.anchor: الكتب } القرآن. { والحكمة } ما تكمل به نفوسهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r3.claim: Wisdom comprises the knowledge and rulings by which people’s souls are perfected.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r3.anchor: ما تكمل به نفوسهم من المعارف والأحكام.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r4.claim: The messenger purifies people from associating partners with God and from sins.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r5.claim: God is invincible in carrying out His will and perfectly orders what He wills.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:128-129#2/r5.anchor: { إنك أنت العزيز } الذي لا يقهر ولا يغلب على ما يريد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r7.claim: Having asked for direct instruction for himself, Ibrāhīm asks that his descendants receive it through the customary intermediary of a messenger.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r7.anchor: ولما طلب ما هو له في منصب النبوة من تعليم الله له المناسك بغير واسطة طلب لذريته مثل ذلك بواسطة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r8.claim: The community among whom the messenger is raised consists of the submitted people descended from Ibrāhīm and his son Ismāʿīl.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r8.anchor: أي الأمة المسلمة التي من ذريتي وذرية ابني إسماعيل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r9.claim: The messenger is Muḥammad, the only descendant of Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl sent with a Book; being one of them makes him more compassionate and easier to follow and support.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r9.anchor: وذلك الرسول هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم , فإنه لم يبعث من ذريتهما بالكتاب غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r10.claim: The prayer is Ibrāhīm’s, the father of the Arabs and noblest of his descendants; the People of the Book are censured for hostility toward the messenger sent to purify them through guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r10.anchor: فهو دعوة إبراهيم عليه السلام أبي العرب وأكرم ذريته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r11.claim: The messenger recites by reading the signs continuously and in sequence.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r12.claim: God’s signs are indicators of him, whether revealed in scripture or inferred from it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r12.anchor: أي علاماتك الدالات عليك أعم من أن يكون نزل بها الكتاب أو استنبطت منه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r13.claim: The Book is complete and comprehensive of every scripture; Biqāʿī evokes the expression that Muḥammad was given comprehensive speech.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r13.anchor: الكتاب } الكامل الشامل لكل كتاب ( أوتيت جوامع الكلم )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r14.claim: Wisdom comprises every command prescribed for them, protecting their worldly and afterlife paths from deviation and ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r14.anchor: وهي كل أمر يشرعه لهم فيحفظهم في صراطي معاشهم ومعادهم من الزيغ المؤدي إلى الضلال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r15.claim: Purification comes after teaching because Islam already provides its foundation, while this community has greater need for instruction.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r15.anchor: فإن أصلها موجود بالإسلام فأخر قوله : { ويزكيهم } أي يطهر قلوبهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r16.claim: In Sūrat al-Jumuʿa, purification precedes teaching because the general unlettered audience first needed release from major shirk to receive knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r16.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه في سورة الجمعة بعثه في الأميين عامة اقتضى المقام تقديم التزكية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r17.claim: In Āl ʿImrān, purification comes first for believers because attachment to worldly spoils caused defeat and is the source of defilement.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r17.anchor: وأما تقديمها في آل عمران مع ذكر البعث للمؤمنين فلاقتضاء الحال بالمعاتبة على الإقبال على الغنائم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r18.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r18.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines al-ʿAzīz as the one who overcomes everything and is overcome by none, and al-Ḥakīm as one whose intended act cannot be undone.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r18.anchor: أي الذي يغلب كل شيء ولا يغالبه شيء , لأن العزة كما قال الحرالي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r19.claim: Knowledge and purified character require arduous struggle and divine ordering; these qualities are especially necessary for a messenger, whose enemies God defeats and whose affairs none can overturn.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p242#2/r19.anchor: فكيف بما يصلح منه للرسالة ؟ وفيه إشارة إلى أنه يكبت أعداء الرسل

DURR-FULL:v1p333/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p333/r3.speaker: العرباض بن سارية
DURR-FULL:v1p333/r3.claim: The Prophet says he was designated the final prophet in the primordial record while Adam was still formed in clay; his mission's beginnings were Abraham's prayer, Jesus's glad tidings, and his mother's vision.
DURR-FULL:v1p333/r3.anchor: عن العرباض بن سارية قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إني عند الله في أم الكتاب لخاتم النبيين وإن آدم لمنجدل في طينته

DURR-FULL:v1p333/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p333/r4.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v1p333/r4.claim: Asked about the beginning of his mission, the Prophet cited Abraham's prayer, Jesus's glad tidings, and his mother's vision of a light illuminating Syrian palaces.
DURR-FULL:v1p333/r4.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال: قلت يا رسول الله ما كان بدء أمرك قال: دعوة إبراهيم وبشرى عيسى ورأت أمي أنه يخرج منها نور أضاءت له قصور الشام

DURR-FULL:v1p333/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p333/r5.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v1p333/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits the Prophet saying that he was Abraham's prayer, uttered while Abraham raised the House's foundations and recited this verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p333/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أنا دعوة إبراهيم

DURR-FULL:v1p334/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r1.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies the people among whom the messenger is raised as Muhammad's community; the prayer was answered and would come to pass at the end of time.
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم} يعني أمة محمد فقيل له: قد استجيب لك

DURR-FULL:v1p334/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r2.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r2.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the messenger as Muhammad.
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r2.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم} قال: هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p334/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r3.claim: Al-Hasan explains wisdom as the Sunna.
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r3.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} قال: السنة

DURR-FULL:v1p334/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r4.claim: Qatada also explains wisdom as the Sunna.
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} قال: الحكمة السنة

DURR-FULL:v1p334/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r5.claim: Qatada says the prayer was fulfilled: a messenger known by name and lineage brought people from darkness to light and guided them to a straight path.
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} قال: الحكمة السنة قال: ففعل ذلك بهم فبعث فيهم رسولا

DURR-FULL:v1p334/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r6.claim: Mak'hul transmits the Prophet saying God gave him the Quran and twice as much wisdom.
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r6.anchor: عن مكحول قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم آتاني الله القرآن ومن الحكمة مثليه

DURR-FULL:v1p334/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains purification as cleansing people of shirk and freeing them from it.
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {يزكيهم} قال: يطهرهم من الشرك ويخلصهم منه

DURR-FULL:v1p334/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r8.claim: Abu al-Aliya says God is mighty in punishment when He punishes and wise in His affair.
DURR-FULL:v1p334/r8.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {العزيز الحكيم} قال: عزيز في نقمته إذا انتقم حكيم في أمره

IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r1.claim: The Prophet says he was already God's final prophet while Adam was still in his clay, and identifies Abraham's supplication as the reason for this.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r1.anchor: سمعت النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يقول : اني عند الله لخاتم النبيين ، وان ادم لمنجدل في طينته

IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the requested messenger is from Muhammad's community; Abraham was told the prayer was answered and would come to pass at the end of time.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r2.anchor: عن أبي العالية قوله : ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهميعني امة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r3.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the messenger as Muhammad.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r3.anchor: عن السدى : وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم و هو محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r4.claim: Qatadah says God answered by sending a messenger known to the people by face and lineage, who brings them from darkness to light and guides them to the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : ربنا و ابعث فيهم رسولا منهم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says God's signs here mean the Qur'an.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : اياته يعني القران

IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r6.claim: Hasan explains the Book as the Qur'an; Yahya ibn Abi Kathir and Muqatil ibn Hayyan are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r6.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : ويعلمهم الكتاب قال : الكتاب : القران

IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas offers an alternative gloss: the Book is writing with the pen.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : الكتاب قال : الخط بالقلم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r8.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r8.claim: Ibn Ishaq says teaching the Book and wisdom means teaching people good and evil so they practice the good, avoid evil, obey God, and shun what displeases Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p236/r8.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق : ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة قال : يعلمهم الخير والشر ليعرفوا الخير فيعلموه والشر فيتقوه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r1.speaker: الحسن، أبو مالك، مقاتل بن حيان، قتادة، يحيى بن أبي كثير
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r1.claim: They interpret the wisdom taught by the Messenger as the Sunna.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة قال : الحكمة حكمة السنة .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r2.claim: Al-Suddi interprets the wisdom taught by the Messenger as prophethood.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r2.anchor: عن السدى قوله : الحكمة يعني النبوة .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r3.speaker: ابن زيد بن أسلم عن أبيه
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd transmits from his father that wisdom means reason in religion.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r3.anchor: عن أبيه قال : الحكمة : العقل في الدين .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r4.claim: Purifying them means, through zakat, obedience to God and sincerity.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس : ويزكيهم يعني بالزكاة طاعة الله والاخلاص .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r5.claim: Al-Aziz means mighty in punishment when He takes vengeance.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية : العزيز يقول : عزيز في نقمته اذا انتقم .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r6.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r6.claim: God is mighty in supporting those who believe in Him against disbelievers when He wills.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r6.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق : العزيز في نصرته ممن كفر به اذا شاء .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r7.claim: Al-Hakim means wise in His command.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r7.anchor: عن أبي العالية : ' العزيز الحكيم ' قال : الحكيم في امره .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r8.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r8.claim: God is wise in His excuse and argument addressed to His servants.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p237/r8.anchor: قال محمد : الحكيم في عذره ، وحجته إلى عباده .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p720/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p720/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p720/r8.claim: Ibrahim's prayer was fulfilled among the Arabs who embraced Islam before and after the Hijra; the small number of exceptions did not break the community, and the next prayer signals this fulfillment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p720/r8.anchor: وقد استجيبت دعوة إبراهيم في المسلمين من العرب الذين تلاحقوا بالإسلام قبل الهجرة وبعدها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r7.claim: The Prophet referred to this prayer when he said, ‘I am the supplication of my father Abraham and the good news of Jesus.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r7.anchor: هذا هو الذي أراد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله «أنا دعوة أبي إبراهيم، وبشرى عيسى»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r8.claim: ‘From among them’ means that the messenger would be known to them, his merit recognized, and he would show them concern, compassion, and care.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r8.anchor: ومعنى منهم أن يعرفوه ويتحققوا فضله ويشفق عليهم ويحرص

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r9.claim: يَتْلُوا may be an accusative adjective describing messenger as one reciting to them, or a circumstantial clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r9.anchor: في موضع نصب نعت لرسول أي تاليا عليهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r10.claim: The signs and the Book are the Qur’an; the Prophet is credited with teaching because he supplies what people investigate and teaches methods of inquiry through what God reveals to him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r10.anchor: والآيات آيات القرآن، والكتاب القرآن، ونسب التعليم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r11.claim: Qatada identifies wisdom as the Sunna and the Prophet’s explanation of the legal rulings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة: الحكمة السنة وبيان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الشرائع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r12.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r12.claim: Malik, as transmitted by Ibn Wahb, identifies wisdom as religious understanding and an inborn comprehension and light from God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r12.anchor: وروى ابن وهب عن مالك: أن الحكمة الفقه في الدين والفهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r13.claim: Yuzakkīhim means to purify them and cultivate them in goodness; zakāt’s sense does not go beyond purification or growth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r13.anchor: ويزكيهم معناه يطهرهم وينميهم بالخير، ومعنى الزكاة لا يخرج عن التطهير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r14.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is the one who overcomes, whose will is carried out and not repelled; al-Ḥakīm places actions correctly and makes them precise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p211#2/r14.anchor: والعزيز الذي يغلب ويتم مراده ولا يرد، والحكيم المصيب مواقع الفعل المحكم لها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r1.speaker: مقاتل والفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r1.claim: One view takes the pronoun in ‘among them’ to refer to Abraham’s descendants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r1.anchor: قولان أحدهما أنها تعود على الذرية قاله مقاتل والفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r2.speaker: مقاتل والفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r2.claim: The other view takes the pronoun to refer to the people of Mecca mentioned in ‘provide for its people’ at 2:126.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r2.anchor: والثاني على أهل مكة في قوله ﴿ وارزق أهله ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r3.anchor: والمراد بالرسول محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد روى أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r4.claim: In a report from Abū Umāma, the Prophet says the beginning of his mission was Abraham’s prayer, Jesus’ good news, and his mother’s vision of a light illuminating Syria’s palaces.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r4.anchor: وقد روى أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قيل يا رسول الله ما كان بدء أمرك قال دعوة أبي إبراهيم وبشري عيسى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the Book as the Quran.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r5.anchor: والكتاب القرآن والحكمة السنة قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r6.claim: One interpretation from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies wisdom as the Sunna.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r6.anchor: والكتاب القرآن والحكمة السنة قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r7.claim: Other explanations reported from Ibn ʿAbbās are fiqh, the lawful and unlawful, or the Quran’s admonitions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r7.anchor: وروي عنه الحكمة الفقه والحلال والحرام ومواعظ القرأن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r8.claim: Wisdom is called ḥikma because it prevents ignorance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r8.anchor: وسميت الحكمة حكمة لأنها تمنع من الجهل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r9.claim: One explanation is that the Messenger collects alms from them and thereby purifies them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r9.anchor: أحدها أن معناه يأخذ الزكاه منهم فيطهرهم بها قاله ابن عباس والفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r10.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r10.claim: Muqātil interprets the phrase as purifying them from polytheism and unbelief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r10.anchor: والثاني يطهرهم من الشرك والكفر قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r11.claim: A third explanation is that the Messenger calls them to what will make them pure.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p146/r11.anchor: والثالث يدعوهم إلى ما يصيرون به أزكياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r1.claim: Abraham's prayer for a messenger among the sanctuary's people was fulfilled in God's decree when Muhammad, from Abraham's descendants, was sent to the unlettered Arabs and to all non-Arabs, humans, and jinn.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r1.anchor: أن يبعث الله فيهم رسولا منهم، أي من ذرية إبراهيم. وقد وافقت هذه الدعوة المستجابة قدر الله السابق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says he was already designated the Seal of the Prophets while Adam lay in clay, and identifies Abraham's prayer, Jesus's glad tidings, and his mother's vision as the first signs of his coming; mothers of prophets likewise see such visions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إني عند الله لخاتم النبيين، وإن آدم لمنجدل في طينته، وسأنبئكم بأول ذلك، دعوة أبي إبراهيم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r3.claim: Asked about the beginning of his mission, the Prophet cites Abraham's prayer, Jesus's glad tidings, and his mother's vision of a light illuminating Syria's palaces.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r3.anchor: لحديث: "دعوة أبي إبراهيم، وبشرى عيسى بن مريم".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r4.claim: The mother's vision is said to have occurred in a dream during pregnancy and spread among her people; Syria's light signifies the faith's stability there, and Syria will be Islam's refuge at the end of time, where Jesus descends at Damascus's eastern white minaret.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r4.anchor: وتخصيص الشام بظهور نوره إشارة إلى استقرار دينه وثبوته ببلاد الشام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r5.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r5.claim: The Prophet's report says a group of his community will remain manifest on the truth, unharmed by opponents until God's command comes; a Bukhari version locates them in Syria.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r5.anchor: لا تزال طائفة من أمتي ظاهرين على الحق لا يضرهم من خذلهم ولا من خالفهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r6.claim: Abraham first publicized Muhammad's name; the final Israelite prophet, Jesus son of Mary, later announced him by name and said a messenger called Ahmad would follow, as quoted from 61:6.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p443#2/r6.anchor: إني رسول الله إليكم مصدقا لما بين يدي من التوراة ومبشرا برسول يأتي من بعدي اسمه أحمد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r1.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the people meant are Muhammad's community; Abraham was told the prayer was answered and would come to pass at the end of time, as al-Suddi and Qatada also say.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r1.anchor: قال (8) أبو جعفر الرازي، عن الربيع بن أنس، عن أبي العالية، في قوله: {ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم} يعني: أمة محمد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة ومقاتل بن حيان وأبو مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r2.claim: Hasan, Qatada, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Abu Malik, and others identify the Book as Quran and wisdom as Sunnah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r2.anchor: قاله الحسن، وقتادة، ومقاتل بن حيان، وأبو مالك وغيرهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r3.claim: Another gloss takes wisdom as understanding in religion; the author says this does not conflict with identifying it as Sunnah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r3.anchor: وقيل: الفهم في الدين. ولا منافاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets purification as obedience to God and sincerity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r4.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: يعني طاعة الله، والإخلاص

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r5.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the messenger teaches people good to practice and evil to avoid, informing them of God's pleasure at obedience and displeasure at disobedience.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق {ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة} قال: يعلمهم الخير فيفعلوه، والشر فيتقوه، ويخبرهم برضاه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r6.claim: God is Mighty, incapable of being thwarted and able to do all things; He is Wise in word and deed, putting things in their proper places with wisdom and justice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p444/r6.anchor: العزيز الذي لا يعجزه شيء، وهو قادر على كل شيء، الحكيم في أفعاله وأقواله

JISHUMI:v1p593/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p593/r1.claim: Al-baʿth means sending or dispatching, as in sending someone as a messenger, and also raising someone from the grave.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r1.anchor: البعث: الإرسال، ومنه بعثه رسولا، وبعثه من قبره.

JISHUMI:v1p593/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p593/r2.claim: Tazkiya means purification; a pure soul is called zakiyya.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r2.anchor: والتزكية: التطهير، يقال: نفس زكية، أي طاهرة،

JISHUMI:v1p593/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p593/r3.claim: The name al-Nafs al-Zakiyya was associated with Muhammad b. ʿAbd Allah b. al-Hasan after reports foretold his death at a place of that name, where he was killed.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r3.anchor: وسمي محمد بن عبد الله بن الحسن بن الحسن النفس الزكية؛ لأخبار ظهرت

JISHUMI:v1p593/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p593/r4.claim: Al-ʿAziz means powerful and unconquerable; the root sense of might is strength, and as a divine attribute it means capable.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r4.anchor: العزيز: القادر الذي لا يغالب، وأصل العزة القوة،

JISHUMI:v1p593/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p593/r5.claim: Other glosses make al-ʿAziz the one whom nothing can thwart or the impregnable; the commentator says these too mean capable as an attribute of essence.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو القادر الذي لا يمتنع عليه شيء، وقيل: المنيع،

JISHUMI:v1p593/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p593/r6.claim: Al-Hakim can mean all-knowing, an attribute of essence, or one who makes his acts precise, an attribute of action.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r6.anchor: وحكيم: بمعنى عالم من صفة الذات، وبمعنى محكم لأفعاله

JISHUMI:v1p593/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p593/r7.claim: After explaining the two patriarchs’ prayer for offspring, the verse turns to their prayer for the Prophet.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r7.anchor: لما بين تعالى دعاءهما للذرية بين دعاءهما لنبينا فقال تعالى:

JISHUMI:v1p593/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p593/r8.claim: The requested messenger is Muhammad, identified with the report that he is Abraham’s prayer and Jesus’s glad tidings in 61:6.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r8.anchor: هو محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم -؛ ولذلك قال: أنا دعوة إبراهيم،

JISHUMI:v1p593/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r9.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وجماعة من أهل العلم
JISHUMI:v1p593/r9.claim: They take “among them” to mean the community mentioned earlier.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r9.anchor: يعني في الأمة التي سبق ذكرها، عن الحسن وقتادة وجماعة من أهل العلم.

JISHUMI:v1p593/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r10.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p593/r10.claim: Abu ʿAli says the prayer concerns descendants around Mecca; only Muhammad fit the description, unlike the prophets of Israel.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r10.anchor: قال أبو علي: لأنه دعاء للذرية التي تكون حول مكة فلم يبعث

JISHUMI:v1p593/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p593/r11.claim: “From them” is glossed either as from the Muslim community or from the people of Mecca; the prayer asks for a guiding prophet who is one of them.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r11.anchor: من الأمة المسلمة، وقيل: من أهل مكة فدعا بشيئين: نبي يهديهم،

JISHUMI:v1p593/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p593/r12.claim: The signs recited to them are glossed as God’s proofs or as the Qur’an; the commentator prefers Qur’an because it directly fits recitation.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r12.anchor: حججك، وقيل: هو القرآن، وهو أولى لتعلقه بالتلاوة (ويعلمهم الكتاب)

JISHUMI:v1p593/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p593/r13.claim: Teaching the Qur’an explains its laws, proofs of divine unity and justice, and other rulings, while recitation first establishes its inimitability and the messenger’s prophethood; the two clauses are not redundant.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r13.anchor: فبالأول تلاوته ليعلموا أنه معجز، وأنه نبي، وبالثاني: يعلم ما يتضمنه

JISHUMI:v1p593/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p593/r14.claim: Another explanation assigns two different descriptions to the Book: it is written, and it is a proof and argument.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r14.anchor: وقيل: وصف الكتاب بصفتين مختلفتين: الأول: أنه مكتوب، والثاني: أنه حجة وبرهان.

JISHUMI:v1p593/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r15.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v1p593/r15.claim: Qatada interprets wisdom as the Sunna.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r15.anchor: (والحكمة) قيل: السنة، عن قتادة. وقيل: المعرفة بالدين

JISHUMI:v1p593/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r16.speaker: مالك بن أنس
JISHUMI:v1p593/r16.claim: Malik b. Anas glosses wisdom as religious understanding and jurisprudence in interpretation.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r16.anchor: وقيل: المعرفة بالدين والفقه في التأويل، عن مالك بن أنس.

JISHUMI:v1p593/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r17.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v1p593/r17.claim: Ibn Zayd says wisdom is knowledge of rulings that can only be learned from a messenger.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r17.anchor: وقيل: العلم بالأحكام التي لا تدرك إلا من جهة الرسول، عن ابن زيد.

JISHUMI:v1p593/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p593/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p593/r18.claim: Other readings make wisdom a quality of the Book itself, describing it as scripture, wisdom, and signs; as knowledge together with practice; or as Qur’anic admonitions and its lawful and forbidden matters.
JISHUMI:v1p593/r18.anchor: وقيل: هو صفة الكتاب كأنه وصفه بأنه كتاب، وأنه حكمة، وأنه آيات،

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r1.claim: “Among them” means this community, and the messenger is Muhammad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r1.anchor: يعني في هذه الأمة { رسولا منهم }

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r2.claim: A reading attributed to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb adds “at the end of them.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r2.anchor: وقيل في قراءة أبي بن كعب { ربنا وابعث في آخرهم رسولا منهم }

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r3.claim: Khalid ibn Maʿdān reports that companions asked the Prophet about himself, and he replied, “I am Abraham’s prayer and Jesus’ glad tidings.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r3.anchor: يا رسول الله أخبرنا عن نفسك , قال : ( نعم , أنا دعوة إبراهيم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r4.claim: One explanation says the messenger recites God’s proof to the people.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r5.claim: The alternative is that he explains their religion to them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r7.claim: Qatāda interprets wisdom as the Sunna.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r7.anchor: أحدهما : أنها السنة , وهو قول قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd takes wisdom as knowledge of religion, understanding it, and following it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r8.anchor: والثاني : أنها المعرفة بالدين , والفقه فيه , والاتباع له , وهو قول ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r9.claim: One explanation is that the messenger purifies people of associating God with idols and worshipping them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r9.anchor: معناه يطهرهم من الشرك بالله وعبادة الأوثان

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r10.claim: Alternatively, following his religion makes them pure in God’s sight.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p191/r10.anchor: يزكيهم بدينه إذا اتبعوه فيكونون به عند الله أزكياء

MUQATIL:2:128-129/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:128-129/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:128-129/r3.claim: In them means among Abraham and Ishmael's descendants, and a messenger from them means Muhammad.
MUQATIL:2:128-129/r3.anchor: فقالا عند ذلك: { ربنا وابعث فيهم } ، يعنى فى ذريتنا { رسولا منهم } ، يعنى محمد

MUQATIL:2:128-129/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:128-129/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:128-129/r4.claim: The messenger recites Quranic verses to them and teaches them the scripture, meaning what is recited to them from the Quran.
