MUQATIL:2:128-129/r4.anchor: يعنى يقرأ عليهم آيات القرآن، { ويعلمهم الكتاب } ، يقول: يعلمهم ما يتلى عليهم من القرآن،

MUQATIL:2:128-129/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:128-129/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:128-129/r5.claim: Wisdom means the admonition in the Quran concerning what is lawful and unlawful; purifying the people means cleansing them of associating partners and disbelief.
MUQATIL:2:128-129/r5.anchor: ثم قال: { والحكمة } ، يعنى الموعظة التي فى القرآن من الحلال والحرام، { ويزكيهم } ، يعنى ويطهرهم من الشرك والكفر،

MUQATIL:2:128-129/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:128-129/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:128-129/r6.claim: God answered Abraham and Ishmael's prayer in 62:2, which Muqatil quotes through the end of that verse.
MUQATIL:2:128-129/r6.anchor: فاستجاب الله له فى سورة الجمعة، فقال:

NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r1.claim: The prayer asks for a messenger from the Muslim community itself; God sent Muhammad among them.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r1.anchor: من أنفسهم فبعث الله فيهم محمدا عليه السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r2.speaker: النبي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r2.claim: The Prophet said he was the prayer of his father Abraham, the glad tidings of Jesus, and his mother’s vision; no grading is stated.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r2.anchor: قال عليه السلام انا دعوة ابى إبراهيم وبشرى عيسى ورؤيا امى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r3.claim: The messenger recites and conveys God’s revelation: proofs of divine oneness and the truthfulness of prophets and messengers.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r3.anchor: يقرأ عليهم ويبلغهم ما توحى إليه من دلائل وحدانيتك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r4.claim: The Book is the Qur’an; wisdom is the Sunna and understanding the Qur’an.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r5.claim: Purifying them means cleansing them of associating partners with God and other defilements.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r6.claim: العزيز is the invincible one who cannot be overcome; الحكيم describes God’s wisdom in what He grants.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p71/r6.anchor: الغالب الذى لا يغلب ﴿ الحكيم ﴾ فيما أوليت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r1.claim: The requested messenger among Abraham's descendants is Muhammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r1.anchor: { ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم } يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r2.speaker: أبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r2.claim: Ubayy reads this as sending a messenger among their later generations.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r2.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي «وابعث في آخرهم رسولا منهم»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r3.speaker: خالد بن معدان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r3.claim: Khalid ibn Ma'dan reports that Companions asked Muhammad about himself; he replied that he was Abraham's prayer and Jesus' glad tidings.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r4.claim: Rasūl means one sent as a messenger and follows faʿūl from risāla.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r4.anchor: و «رسولا» أي مرسلا وهو فعول من الرسالة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbari suggests rasūl derives from a she-camel called marsāl or rasla because she travels easily ahead of the others.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r5.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: يشبه أن يكون أصله من قولهم: ناقة مرسال ورسلة إذا كانت سهلة السير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r6.claim: Dispatched groups are rusul, their plural arsāl, arrivals in sequence are arsālan, and milk is rasl because it flows from the udder.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r6.anchor: ويقال للجماعة المهملة المرسلة: رسل، وجمعه أرسال. ويقال: جاء القوم أرسالا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r8.speaker: مالك وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r8.claim: Malik, transmitted by Ibn Wahb, and Ibn Zayd explain wisdom as religious knowledge, interpretive understanding, and an innate insight and light from God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r8.anchor: «الحكمة»: المعرفة بالدين، والفقه في التأويل، والفهم الذي هو سجية ونور من الله تعالى قاله مالك، ورواه عنه ابن وهب، وقاله ابن زيد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r9.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r9.claim: Qatada interprets wisdom as the Sunna and clarification of religious laws.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r10.claim: Another explanation restricts wisdom to judgment and adjudication; al-Qurtubi says the meanings are close.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r10.anchor: وقيل: الحكم والقضاء خاصة والمعنى متقارب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r11.claim: Teaching is attributed to the Prophet because he supplies matters for reflection and teaches how to reason through revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r11.anchor: ونسب التعليم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من حيث هو يعطي الأمور التي ينظر فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r12.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r12.claim: Ibn Jurayj and others explain purification as cleansing people from the stain of associationism.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r12.anchor: أي يطهرهم من وضر الشرك عن ابن جريج وغيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r13.claim: Zakāh carries the lexical sense of purification.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r14.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r14.claim: One explanation distinguishes recited wording as signs, their meanings as the Book, and God's intended rulings as wisdom, including general/specific and qualified/unqualified forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r14.anchor: وقيل: إن الآيات تلاوة ظاهر الألفاظ. والكتاب معاني الألفاظ. والحكمة الحكم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r15.claim: Al-ʿAzīz means inviolable: no one can reach or overcome Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r15.anchor: و { العزيز } معناه المنيع الذي لا ينال ولا يغالب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r16.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r16.claim: Ibn Kaysan explains al-ʿAzīz as the One whom nothing can defeat, citing that nothing in heaven or earth can thwart God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r16.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: معناه الذي لا يعجزه شيء دليله:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r17.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r17.claim: Al-Kisa'i defines al-ʿAzīz as the dominant, citing the wording of being overcome in dispute and the proverb that the victor takes the spoils.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r18.claim: Another gloss takes al-ʿAzīz to mean the One without an equal, supported by the declaration that nothing resembles Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129/r18.anchor: وقيل: «العزيز» الذي لا مثل له بيانه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:129#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129#2/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi supports the gloss of al-ʿAzīz as the One without an equal with “nothing is like Him,” and says he explained this name elsewhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:129#2/r1.anchor: [الشورى: 11]. وقد زدنا هذا المعنى بيانا في اسمه العزيز

QASHANI:2:128-129/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:128-129/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:128-129/r4.anchor: هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولهذا قال عليه السلام:

QASHANI:2:128-129/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:128-129/r5.speaker: النبي محمد
QASHANI:2:128-129/r5.claim: Muhammad says he is Abraham's prayer, Jesus' glad tidings, and his mother's vision; she saw a light emerge and illuminate Syria's palaces.
QASHANI:2:128-129/r5.anchor: هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولهذا قال عليه السلام:

RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r1.claim: The requested messenger is from the same descendants as the Muslim community in the preceding prayer; that description fits Muhammad's community.
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r1.anchor: لا شبهة في أن قوله : { ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا } يريد

RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r2.claim: A messenger among them completes their religion and law and calls them to remain steadfast in Islam.
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r2.anchor: أن يكون فيهم رسول يكمل لهم الدين والشرع

RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r3.claim: Having a messenger from their own descendants gives them greater honor and religious standing than a messenger from outside their lineage.
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r3.anchor: لأن الرسول والمرسل إليه إذا كانا معا من ذريته

RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r4.claim: A messenger from among them makes it easier to know his truthfulness and trustworthiness because they know his origin and upbringing.
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r4.anchor: إذا كان منهم فإنهم يعرفون مولده ومنشأه

RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r5.claim: A messenger from their own people is more solicitous for their welfare and compassionate toward them than an outsider would be.
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r5.anchor: إذا كان منهم كان أحرص الناس على خيرهم

RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r6.claim: Abraham sought to establish religion for his descendants both immediately and in the future, believing his aim would be most fully realized through them, with added joy and honor in that outcome.
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r6.anchor: عمارة الدين في الحال وفي المستقبل

RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r7.speaker: إجماع المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r7.claim: Razi identifies Muhammad as the messenger and cites the commentators' consensus as proof.

RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r8.claim: Muhammad is reported to have said, “I am Abraham's prayer and Jesus' glad tidings”; Razi identifies Abraham's prayer with this verse and Jesus' glad tidings with 61:6.
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r8.anchor: ما روي عنه عليه السلام أنه قال

RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r9.claim: Abraham prayed in Mecca for descendants there and nearby, and God sent no messenger to its people and surroundings except Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v4p59/r9.anchor: إن إبراهيم عليه السلام إنما دعا بهذا الدعاء بمكة

RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r1.claim: One explanation for pairing Abraham with Muhammad in blessings is that Abraham prayed for Muhammad here, so God repaid the intimate friend by keeping his name on the community's tongues.
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r1.anchor: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام دعا لمحمد عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r2.claim: Another explanation is that Abraham's prayer for lasting good praise (26:84) was answered by joining his name to Muhammad's in the latter's community.
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r2.anchor: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام سأل ذلك ربه بقوله

RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r3.claim: A third explanation calls Abraham father of the religious community (22:78) and Muhammad a father of mercy, citing Ibn Masud's reading, 9:128, and the Prophet's saying that he is like a father to believers.

RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r4.claim: The Prophet said he was like a father to the believers in compassion and mercy, another reason to pair him with Abraham in blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r4.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : ( إنما أنا لكم مثل الوالد )

RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r5.claim: A fourth explanation pairs Abraham, herald of the pilgrimage (22:27), with Muhammad, herald of faith (3:193), in remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v4p60/r5.anchor: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام كان منادي الشريعة في الحج

RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r1.claim: Razi gives two meanings for the signs recited: the Qur'an revealed to Muhammad, since that is what he recited, or proofs of the Creator and His attributes, which he reminded people of and called them to believe.
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r1.anchor: أنها الفرقان الذي أنزل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r2.claim: Teaching the Book means directing people to recite it and teaching its meanings and realities.
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r2.anchor: والمراد أنه يأمرهم بتلاوة الكتاب ويعلمهم معاني الكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r3.claim: Recitation preserves the Qur'an's wording through mass transmission, safeguards it against textual corruption, displays its miraculous wording and arrangement, and is itself worship, including in prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r3.anchor: ومنها أن يكون لفظه ونظمه معجزا لمحمد

RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r4.claim: The highest purpose is teaching the Book's proofs, rulings, meanings, wisdom, and secrets; therefore recitation is followed by teaching its deeper realities.
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r4.anchor: الحكمة العظمى والمقصود الأشرف تعليم ما فيه من الدلائل والأحكام

RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r5.claim: Wisdom is rightness in speech and action; one is wise only by combining both and placing each thing where it belongs.
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r5.anchor: الإصابة في القول والعمل ، ولا يسمى حكيما إلا من اجتمع له الأمران

RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r6.claim: The word may derive from ahkamtu, “I restrained”: wisdom restrains ignorance and error through sound speech and action.
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r6.anchor: أصلها من أحكمت الشيء أي رددته

RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r7.speaker: الفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r7.claim: Al-Qaffal reports a philosophers' definition of wisdom as resembling God to the extent humanly possible.
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r7.anchor: قال القفال : وعبر بعض الفلاسفة عن الحكمة

RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r8.speaker: مالك
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r8.claim: Malik, in an answer to Ibn Wahb, defines wisdom as knowledge of religion, understanding it, and following it.

RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r9.speaker: الشافعي وقتادة
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r9.claim: Al-Shafi'i and Qatada identify wisdom as the Prophet's Sunnah.
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r9.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : الحكمة سنة رسول الله

RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r10.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r10.claim: Al-Shafi'i's followers argue that because the verse separately mentions reciting and teaching the Book before wisdom, wisdom must be something outside the Book, namely the Sunnah; an objection asks why it could not mean rational proofs of monotheism, justice, and prophecy.
RAZI-FULL:v4p60#2/r10.anchor: أنه تعالى ذكر تلاوة الكتاب أولا وتعليمه ثانيا

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r1.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r1.claim: In response to the objection, al-Shafi'i's followers say that reason independently receives rational proofs, so wisdom here should mean knowledge not obtained except through revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r1.anchor: لأن العقول مستقبلة بذلك فحمل هذا اللفظ

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes wisdom as distinguishing truth from falsehood, a verbal noun meaning judgment; the messenger teaches God's revealed Book and the rulings and judgments God teaches him.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r2.anchor: الفصل بين الحق والباطل ، وهو مصدر بمعنى الحكم

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r3.claim: One interpretation takes “Book” as the unambiguous verses and “wisdom” as the ambiguous verses.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r3.anchor: أراد به الآيات المحكمة . ( والحكمة ) أراد بها الآيات المتشابهات

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the Book as its rulings and wisdom as teaching the rationale, benefits, and interests served by those laws.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r4.anchor: أي يعلمهم ما فيه من الأحكام . ( والحكمة ) أراد بها أنه يعلمهم حكمة

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r5.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r5.claim: Some say all these descriptions are attributes of the Qur'an: it is signs, a Book, and wisdom.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r5.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : الكل صفات الكتاب كأنه تعالى وصفه

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r6.claim: Human perfection requires knowing truth for its own sake and knowing good in order to act on it; purification follows the mention of virtue by removing vice and deficiency.

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r7.claim: Since a messenger does not coercively control people's inner lives, purification means his other efforts—warnings, promises, exhortation, reminders, and practical engagement—strengthen their motives to believe and do good; Razi prefers this over the alternative.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r7.anchor: الأول : ما يفعله سوى التلاوة وتعليم الكتاب والحكمة

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r8.claim: An alternative is that the messenger testifies to their purity on Judgment Day, as a person certifying witnesses; Razi says the first interpretation better fits Abraham's prayer for his descendants' salvation.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r8.anchor: الثاني : يزكيهم ، يشهد لهم بأنهم أزكياء يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r9.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says the messenger purifies them from polytheism; Razi infers that Ismail's descendants included ignorant polytheists whom the messenger would make wise after ignorance.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r9.anchor: قال الحسن : يزكيهم : يطهرهم من شركهم

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets purification as obedience to God and sincerity.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r10.anchor: وثانيها : التزكية هي الطاعة لله والإخلاص عن ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r11.claim: Another interpretation takes purification as removal of polytheism and other impurities, as in 7:157.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r11.anchor: ويزكيهم عن الشرك وسائر الأرجاس ، كقوله

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r12.claim: The closing praise calls God unconquerably powerful and all-knowing; His knowledge and power make His acts sound and free of absurdity, enabling answered prayer, messengers, and revelation.

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r13.claim: Aziz is an essential attribute when it means power over things and invulnerability to need or humiliation, since God has no needs and none can block His will.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r13.anchor: العزيز من صفات الذات إذا أريد اقتداره على الأشياء

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r14.claim: If “aziz” means invulnerability to another's control and “hakim” means wise acts, both are attributes of action; essence attributes are eternal and cannot have opposites, while action attributes are relative and depend on effects.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r14.anchor: إذا أريد بالعزة كمال العزة وهو الامتناع من استيلاء الغير عليه

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r15.speaker: النظام
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r15.claim: Al-Nazzam argues God cannot perform a vile act: essential wisdom excludes folly, and an impossible act cannot be within divine power.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r15.anchor: واحتج النظام على أنه تعالى غير قادر على القبيح

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r16.speaker: النظام
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r16.claim: Al-Nazzam reasons that if God's wisdom could be replaced by its opposite, Godhood without wisdom would result, which is impossible; wisdom and foolishness are intuitively incompatible, so God cannot do what is vile.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r16.anchor: لو لم يجب ذلك لجاز تبدله بنقيضه

RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r17.speaker: النظام
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r17.claim: Al-Nazzam further argues that wisdom is intuitively incompatible with foolish action, and what entails an impossibility cannot be within divine power.
RAZI-FULL:v4p61/r17.anchor: الحكمة تنافي فعل السفه فذلك أيضا معلوم بالبديهة

RAZI-FULL:v4p62/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p62/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p62/r1.claim: Razi answers al-Nazzam that on Razi's doctrine none of God's acts is folly, so the objection disappears.
RAZI-FULL:v4p62/r1.anchor: أما على مذهبنا فليس شيء من الأفعال سفها منه فزال السؤال

STUDYQURAN:2:129/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r1.claim: The messenger requested in Abraham’s prayer is realized in 2:151, where the Prophet is described in terms identical to this verse.
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r1.anchor: The response to this prayer for a messenger is realized in v. 151, where the Prophet is described in terms identical to those in this verse.

STUDYQURAN:2:129/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r2.claim: The Book is most often understood as the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r2.anchor: The Book is most often taken to be the Quran

STUDYQURAN:2:129/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r3.claim: Wisdom is understood as the Sunnah, the Prophet’s exemplary sayings and actions.
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r3.anchor: the Wisdom is understood to be the Sunnah (the exemplary sayings and doings of the Prophet)

STUDYQURAN:2:129/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r4.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r4.claim: Alternatively, Wisdom means knowledge and understanding of religion more generally.
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r4.anchor: or more generally knowledge and understanding of the religion (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:2:129/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r5.claim: The Book and Wisdom pairing has broader Quranic use, also appearing in connection with Jesus, the Children of Israel, and Abraham’s House.
STUDYQURAN:2:129/r5.anchor: although the pairing of the Book and Wisdom has more universal import in the Quran and is also used in connection with Jesus (3:48; 5:110), the Children of Israel (45:16), and the House of Abraham (4:54).

TAB-FULL:v2p573/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r1.speaker: رسول الله
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r1.claim: The Prophet said he was the prayer of Abraham and the good news of Jesus.
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r1.anchor: يا رسول الله أخبرنا عن نفسك. قال؛ «نعم، أنا دعوة أبي إبراهيم، وبشرى عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم»

TAB-FULL:v2p573/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r2.speaker: رسول الله
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r2.claim: Al-Irbad reports the Prophet’s statement that he was foreordained as the seal of prophets while Adam was still in clay; the report also identifies him as Abraham’s prayer, Jesus’s announced good news, and his mother’s vision.
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r2.anchor: عن العرباض بن سارية السلمي، قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " إني عند الله في أم الكتاب خاتم النبيين

TAB-FULL:v2p573/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r3.claim: Qatada says God answered by sending a messenger known by face and lineage, bringing the people from darkness to light and guiding them to the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy.
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: " قوله: {ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم} [البقرة: 129] ففعل الله ذلك، فبعث فيهم رسولا من أنفسهم يعرفون وجهه ونسبه

TAB-FULL:v2p573/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r4.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the requested messenger as Muhammad.
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r4.anchor: عن السدي: " {ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم} [البقرة: 129] هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v2p573/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r5.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r5.claim: Al-Rabiʿ also identifies him as Muhammad and says Abraham was told his prayer was answered and the messenger would appear at the end of time.
TAB-FULL:v2p573/r5.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع: " {ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم} [البقرة: 129] هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقيل له: قد استجيب ذلك

TAB-FULL:v2p576/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the Book as the Quran.

TAB-FULL:v2p576/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r2.claim: Qatada identifies wisdom as the Sunnah.

TAB-FULL:v2p576/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r3.speaker: مالك
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r3.claim: Malik defines wisdom as knowledge of religion, understanding it, and following it.
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r3.anchor: قلت لمالك: ما الحكمة؟ قال: «المعرفة بالدين، والفقه في الدين، والاتباع له»

TAB-FULL:v2p576/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd calls wisdom the religion known through the Prophet and reason in religion; it is a light God places in the heart, and signs without wisdom do not benefit their recipient.
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r4.anchor: قال: الحكمة: الدين الذي لا يعرفونه إلا به صلى الله عليه وسلم يعلمهم إياها، قال: والحكمة: العقل في الدين

TAB-FULL:v2p576/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r5.claim: Al-Tabari’s preferred meaning is knowledge of God’s rulings that can only be known through the Prophet’s explanation.
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r5.anchor: والصواب من القول عندنا في الحكمة، أنها العلم بأحكام الله التي لا يدرك علمها إلا ببيان الرسول

TAB-FULL:v2p576/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r6.claim: He derives الحكمة from الحكم, judgment separating truth from falsehood, and explains حكيم as accurate in speech and action.
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r6.anchor: وهو عندي مأخوذ من الحكم الذي بمعنى الفصل بين الحق والباطل بمنزلة الجلسة والقعدة من الجلوس والقعود

TAB-FULL:v2p576/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r7.claim: The prayer asks for a messenger to teach them God’s revealed Book, His judgments, and the rulings He teaches the messenger.
TAB-FULL:v2p576/r7.anchor: ويعلمهم كتابك الذي تنزله عليهم، وفصل قضائك، وأحكامك التي تعلمه إياها

TAB-FULL:v2p578/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p578/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p578/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains their purification as obedience to God and sincerity.
TAB-FULL:v2p578/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {يتلو عليهم آياتك ويزكيهم} ، قال: يعني بالزكاة، طاعة الله والإخلاص

TAB-FULL:v2p578/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p578/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v2p578/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the messenger purifies them from shirk and frees them of it.
TAB-FULL:v2p578/r2.anchor: قال ابن جريج: " قوله: {ويزكيهم} [البقرة: 129] ، قال: يطهرهم من الشرك ويخلصهم منه

TABATABAI:2:128-129/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:128-129/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:128-129/r4.claim: Al-Tabataba'i identifies the requested messenger as Muhammad; the Prophet said, “I am Abraham's prayer.”
TABATABAI:2:128-129/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى { ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم } الخ، دعوة للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:2:125-129#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:125-129#9/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:125-129#9/r2.claim: Al-Zubayri reports al-Sadiq’s answer that Muhammad’s community means Banu Hashim; Abraham and Ishmael asked for a Muslim community among their descendants, a messenger from them, and protection from idolatry, grounding the Imams in Abraham’s line.
TABATABAI:2:125-129#9/r2.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن الزبيري عن أبى عبد الله عليه السلام قال قلت له أخبرني عن أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من هم؟

TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r1.claim: Abraham asked for a Muslim community specifically from his and Ishmael’s descendants; the following request for a messenger identifies it with Muhammad’s community, not all his addressees or believers.
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r1.anchor: ومن المعلوم من ذيل دعوته ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم، أن هذه الأمة المسلمة هي أمة محمد

TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r6.claim: The Imams and the Muslim community in Abraham’s prayer are one group, descended from Abraham.
TABATABAI:2:125-129#10/r6.anchor: أي إنهما واحد، وهما من ذرية إبراهيم كما مر بيانه

TABRISI:2:129/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:129/r1.claim: Al-ʿAzīz can mean unconquerable, or capable of anything He wills with nothing able to prevent Him; the root also conveys victory, hardness, rarity, and honor through association.
TABRISI:2:129/r1.anchor: الذي لا يغالب وقيل هو القادر الذي لا يمتنع عليه شيء

TABRISI:2:129/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:129/r2.claim: Al-Ḥakīm means the one who directs and makes creation well, an attribute of action; it can also mean all-knowing, an attribute of essence.
TABRISI:2:129/r2.anchor: والحكيم معناه المدبر الذي يحكم الصنع ويحسن التدبير فعلى هذا يكون من صفات الفعل وبكون بمعنى العليم

TABRISI:2:129/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:129/r3.claim: Ibʿath is a verbal clause coordinated with tab; fīhim attaches to ibʿath or to an omitted ‘messenger being among them’ and then functions circumstantially.
TABRISI:2:129/r3.anchor: ابعث جملة فعلية معطوفة على تب فيهم تتعلق بابعث ويجوز أن تتعلق بمحذوف تقديره رسولا كائنا فيهم

TABRISI:2:129/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:129/r4.claim: Yatlū is accusative as an adjective of rasūlan, while ʿalayhim attaches to yatlū.
TABRISI:2:129/r4.anchor: ويتلو منصوب الموضع بكونه صفة قوله

TABRISI:2:129/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:129/r5.claim: Fīhim refers to the Muslim community among Abraham’s descendants, especially his Meccan descendants; the messenger is Muhammad, the only one sent from them.
TABRISI:2:129/r5.anchor: الضمير في قولهم فيهم يرجع إلى الأمة المسلمة التي سأل الله إبراهيم أن يجعلهم من ذريته

TABRISI:2:129/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وجماعة من العلماء
TABRISI:2:129/r6.claim: Ḥasan, Qatāda, and other scholars identify the requested messenger as Muhammad, who said he was Abraham’s prayer and Jesus’ good tidings, referring to Jesus’ prediction of a messenger named Aḥmad.
TABRISI:2:129/r6.anchor: وهو قول الحسن وقتادة وجماعة من العلماء

TABRISI:2:129/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:129/r7.claim: Reciting God’s signs means reading the revelations He sends down to the messenger.
TABRISI:2:129/r7.anchor: أي يقرأ عليهم آياتك التي توحي بها إليه

TABRISI:2:129/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:129/r8.claim: The Book is the Qurʾan; teaching it is not redundant with recitation, since recitation shows its miraculous proof of prophethood while teaching explains monotheism, its evidence, and the law.
TABRISI:2:129/r8.anchor: وهذا لا يعد من التكرار لأنه خص الأول بالتلاوة ليعلموا بذلك أنه معجز دال على صدقه ونبوته

TABRISI:2:129/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r9.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:129/r9.claim: Qatāda interprets wisdom here as the Sunna.
TABRISI:2:129/r9.anchor: قيل هي ها هنا السنة عن قتادة

TABRISI:2:129/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r10.speaker: مالك بن أنس
TABRISI:2:129/r10.claim: Mālik ibn Anas explains wisdom as knowledge of religion and understanding its interpretation.
TABRISI:2:129/r10.anchor: وقيل المعرفة بالدين والفقه في التأويل عن مالك بن أنس

TABRISI:2:129/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:2:129/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd takes wisdom as knowledge of rulings that can be learned only from the messengers.
TABRISI:2:129/r11.anchor: وقيل العلم بالأحكام التي لا يدرك علمها إلا من قبل الرسل عن ابن زيد

TABRISI:2:129/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r12.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:129/r12.claim: One grammatical reading makes wisdom an adjective of the Book, so it is characterized as Book, wisdom, and signs.
TABRISI:2:129/r12.anchor: وقيل إنه صفة للكتاب كأنه وصفه بأنه كتاب وأنه حكمة وأنه آيات

TABRISI:2:129/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r13.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:129/r13.claim: Another view calls wisdom a light God places in the heart, enabling understanding as eyesight enables seeing.
TABRISI:2:129/r13.anchor: وقيل الحكمة شيء يجعله الله في القلب ينوره الله به كما ينور البصر

TABRISI:2:129/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r14.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:2:129/r14.claim: Muqātil interprets wisdom as Qurʾanic admonitions and knowledge of its lawful and prohibited matters.
TABRISI:2:129/r14.anchor: وقيل هي مواعظ القرآن وحرامه وحلاله عن مقاتل وكل حسن

TABRISI:2:129/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:129/r15.claim: The author says the messenger makes people obedient and sincere; zakāʾ means obedience and sincerity toward God.
TABRISI:2:129/r15.anchor: والزكاء هو الطاعة والإخلاص لله سبحانه عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:129/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r16.speaker: ابن جريج
TABRISI:2:129/r16.claim: Ibn Jurayj says purification means cleansing people of idolatry.
TABRISI:2:129/r16.anchor: وقيل معناه يطهرهم من الشرك ويخلصهم منه عن ابن جريج

TABRISI:2:129/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r17.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:2:129/r17.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī interprets purification as calling people to faith and righteous acts through which they become pure.
TABRISI:2:129/r17.anchor: وقيل معناه يستدعيهم إلى فعل ما يزكون به من الإيمان والصلاح عن الجبائي

TABRISI:2:129/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129/r18.speaker: الأصم
TABRISI:2:129/r18.claim: Al-Aṣamm says purification means the messenger will testify on Judgment Day that they were pure, when every soul is judged by what it earned.
TABRISI:2:129/r18.anchor: وقيل يشهد لهم بأنهم أزكياء يوم القيامة إذا شهد على كل نفس بما كسبت عن الأصم

TABRISI:2:129#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:129#2/r1.claim: The names mean complete power and majesty, and mastery over the wonders of creation; they suit the prayer because God can answer and knows hidden thoughts and what benefits people.
TABRISI:2:129#2/r1.anchor: أي القوي في كمال قدرتك المنيع في جلال عظمتك المحكم لبدائع صنعتك وإنما ذكر هاتين الصفتين لاتصالهما بالدعاء

TABRISI:2:129#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:129#2/r2.claim: The prayer asks for all conditions of prophethood: recitation entails conveying revelation, teaching entails explaining it, and wisdom entails the Sunna.
TABRISI:2:129#2/r2.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن إبراهيم وإسماعيل ع دعوا لنبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بجميع شرائط النبوة

TABRISI:2:129#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:129#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:129#2/r3.claim: The prayer also seeks divine grace for the community, enabling them to hold to scripture and law and become pure; because Ishmael made the prayer, the promised prophet is his descendant, Muhammad, the only prophet from Ishmael’s line.
TABRISI:2:129#2/r3.anchor: فصاروا أزكياء وهذا لأن الدعاء صدر من إسماعيل

THALABI:v1p275/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p275/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p275/r10.claim: The people among whom the messenger is sent are the Muslim community descended from Abraham and Ishmael.
THALABI:v1p275/r10.anchor: ربنا وابعث فيهم أي في الأمة المسلمة من ذرية إبراهيم وإسماعيل

THALABI:v1p275/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p275/r11.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p275/r11.claim: Another explanation identifies them as the people of Mecca.
THALABI:v1p275/r11.anchor: وقيل: في أهل مكة رسولا أي مرسلا

THALABI:v1p275/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p275/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p275/r12.claim: Rasūlan means a messenger and is formed on the faʿūl pattern from risāla.
THALABI:v1p275/r12.anchor: رسولا أي مرسلا وهو فعول من الرسالة

THALABI:v1p275/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p275/r13.speaker: ابن الأنباري
THALABI:v1p275/r13.claim: Ibn al-Anbari suggests the word may derive from a camel described as easy-going and moving ahead; a group sent out is rusul, plural arsāl, and people coming successively arrive irsālan.
THALABI:v1p275/r13.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: يشبه أن يكون أصله من قولهم ناقة مرسال ورسله

THALABI:v1p275/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p275/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p275/r14.claim: Milk is also called rasl because it is sent flowing from the udder.
THALABI:v1p275/r14.anchor: ومنه قيل للبن رسلا لأنه يرسل من الضرع

THALABI:v1p275/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p275/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p275/r15.claim: Yatlu means recites, and God’s signs here mean His Book; āya itself denotes a sign.
THALABI:v1p275/r15.anchor: يتلوا يقرأ عليهم آياتك كتابك جمع الآية وهي العلامة

THALABI:v1p275/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p275/r16.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p275/r16.claim: Another definition of an āya is a group of letters.

THALABI:v1p275/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p275/r17.speaker: الشيباني
THALABI:v1p275/r17.claim: Al-Shaybani cites the expression خرج القوم بما فيهم, meaning the people went out with all their company, as evidence for āya as a collective group.
THALABI:v1p275/r17.anchor: وقال الشيباني: هي قولهم: خرج القوم بما فيهم أي بجماعتهم

THALABI:v1p275/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p275/r18.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p275/r18.claim: Some take āyāt here as the Book, coordinated with wisdom despite the difference in wording; a verse by al-Hutayʾa supports such coordination.
THALABI:v1p275/r18.anchor: فقال بعضهم: الآية هاهنا الكتاب فنسق عليه خلاف اللفظين كقول الحطيئة

THALABI:v1p276/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r1.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v1p276/r1.claim: Mujahid defines wisdom as understanding the Quran.

THALABI:v1p276/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r2.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v1p276/r2.claim: Muqatil says wisdom comprises the Quran’s admonitions, rulings, and clarification of lawful and unlawful things.
THALABI:v1p276/r2.anchor: مقاتل: هي مواعظ القرآن وما فيه من الأحكام وبيان الحلال والحرام

THALABI:v1p276/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
THALABI:v1p276/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba defines wisdom as knowledge and action; a person is not wise without both.
THALABI:v1p276/r3.anchor: ابن قتيبة: هي العلم والعمل ولا يسمى الرجل حكيما حتى يجمعهما

THALABI:v1p276/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r4.speaker: أبو بكر محمد بن الحسن البريدي
THALABI:v1p276/r4.claim: Al-Buraydi calls any word that admonishes, restrains, guides to virtue, or forbids wrongdoing wisdom; he cites the Prophetic saying that some poetry is wisdom.
THALABI:v1p276/r4.anchor: وعن أبي بكر محمد بن الحسن البريدي: كل كلمة وعظتك أو زجرتك أودعتك إلى مكرمة

THALABI:v1p276/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v1p276/r5.claim: The Prophet says that some poetry contains wisdom, cited in support of al-Buraydi’s definition.
THALABI:v1p276/r5.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن من الشعر لحكمة»

THALABI:v1p276/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن يعقوب
THALABI:v1p276/r6.claim: Abu Jaʿfar defines wisdom as any correct saying that yields sound action or a sound state.
THALABI:v1p276/r6.anchor: وعن أبي جعفر محمد بن يعقوب: الحكمة كل صواب من القول ورث فعلا صحيحا

THALABI:v1p276/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r7.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
THALABI:v1p276/r7.claim: Yahya ibn Muʿadh calls wisdom a troop sent by God into the hearts of knowers to cool the heat of worldly life.
THALABI:v1p276/r7.anchor: يحيى بن معاذ: الحكمة جند من جنود الله يرسلها إلى قلوب العارفين حتى يروح

THALABI:v1p276/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r8.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p276/r8.claim: One definition is putting things in their proper places.

THALABI:v1p276/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r9.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p276/r9.claim: Another definition equates wisdom and judgment with whatever one is obliged to do.
THALABI:v1p276/r9.anchor: وقيل: الحكمة والحكم كلما وجب عليك فعله

THALABI:v1p276/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r10.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v1p276/r10.claim: An unattributed poem uses ḥukm for what is incumbent: silence is right action, though few practice it.
THALABI:v1p276/r10.anchor: قال الشاعر: قد قلت قولا لم يعنف قائله … الصمت حكم وقليل فاعله

THALABI:v1p276/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r11.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p276/r11.claim: Another reported interpretation takes wisdom to mean idolatry and sins.

THALABI:v1p276/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r12.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p276/r12.claim: Another reported interpretation takes wisdom to mean collecting the zakat on their property.

THALABI:v1p276/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r13.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v1p276/r13.claim: Ibn Kaysan says the community will testify on Judgment Day to the prophets’ faithful delivery, as 2:143 states.
THALABI:v1p276/r13.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: يشهد لهم يوم القيامة بالعدالة إذا شهدوا الأنبياء بالبلاغ

THALABI:v1p276/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p276/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas defines al-ʿAzīz as the one without equal, citing 42:11.
THALABI:v1p276/r14.anchor: ابن عباس: العزيز الذي لا يوجد مثله، بيانه قوله: ليس كمثله شيء

THALABI:v1p276/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r15.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v1p276/r15.claim: Al-Kalbi defines al-ʿAzīz as the avenger of whomever He wills, citing 3:4.
THALABI:v1p276/r15.anchor: الكلبي: العزيز المنتقم ممن يشاء بيانه قوله والله عزيز ذو انتقام

THALABI:v1p276/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r16.speaker: الكسائي
THALABI:v1p276/r16.claim: Al-Kisaʾi defines al-ʿAzīz as the one who prevails, citing the language of 38:23.
THALABI:v1p276/r16.anchor: الكسائي: العزيز الغالب بيانه قوله وعزني في الخطاب

THALABI:v1p276/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r17.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p276/r17.claim: He cites an otherwise unexplained proverb, من عزيز, in connection with the word.

THALABI:v1p276/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r18.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v1p276/r18.claim: Ibn Kaysan defines al-ʿAzīz as the one nothing can disable, citing 35:44.
THALABI:v1p276/r18.anchor: ابن كيسان: العزيز الذي لا يعجزه شيء بيانه قوله: وما كان الله ليعجزه من شيء

THALABI:v1p276/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r19.speaker: المفضل بن سلمة
THALABI:v1p276/r19.claim: Al-Mufaddal ibn Salama defines al-ʿAzīz as inaccessible and unassailable: no hand reaches Him, no command is refused, and no will is defeated; he cites 11:107.
THALABI:v1p276/r19.anchor: المفضل بن سلمة: العزيز المنيع الذي لا تناله الأيدي فلا يرد له أمر

THALABI:v1p276/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r20.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p276/r20.claim: Another explanation takes al-ʿAzīz as al-Muʿizz, treating faʿīl as the pattern mufʿil; 3:26 is cited.
THALABI:v1p276/r20.anchor: وقيل: بمعنى المعز فعيل بمعنى مفعل بيانه قوله وتعز من تشاء

THALABI:v1p276/r21.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r21.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p276/r21.claim: Another explanation is the strong one, supported by 36:14, where God strengthened the messengers with a third.
THALABI:v1p276/r21.anchor: وقيل: هو القوي بيانه قوله فعززنا بثالث أي قوينا

THALABI:v1p276/r22.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p276/r22.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p276/r22.claim: The root sense of ʿizza is strength or hardness; Arabic says camel flesh hardened and عز علي for something difficult or heavy to bear.
THALABI:v1p276/r22.anchor: فأصل العزة في اللغة الشدة يقال تعزز لحم الناقة إذا اشتد

THALABI:v1p278/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p278/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v1p278/r1.claim: The Prophet says his status as the last prophet was recorded in the Mother of the Book while Adam was still being formed; he links his advent to Abraham’s prayer, Jesus’s glad tidings, and his mother’s vision of light illuminating Syria’s palaces.
THALABI:v1p278/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إني عبد الله في أم الكتاب لخاتم النبيين وإن آدم لمجدل في طينة وسوف أنبئكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says fīhim means among my descendants; the pronoun can refer either to Abraham’s descendants or to the community called a Muslim nation, both identified here as Arabs descended from Abraham.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: في ولدي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the requested messenger from among them as Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد محمدا - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r3.claim: God answered Abraham’s prayer by sending Muhammad from among his people as the master of the prophets.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r3.anchor: فاستجاب الله دعاءه، وبعث فيهم رسولا من أنفسهم، محمدا سيد الأنبياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r4.claim: The Prophet says his status as the Seal of Prophets was written in the Mother of the Book while Adam was still being formed; this was Abraham’s prayer, Jesus’ good news in 61:6, and his mother’s vision of a light illuminating Syrian palaces.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p323/r4.anchor: لذلك قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Book is the revealed Qurʾan and what it contains of duties, rulings, Prophetic practices, and the laws of earlier prophets.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد القرآن الذي أنزل عليه، وما فيه من الفرائض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r2.claim: On Ibn ʿAbbās’s reading, wisdom is the Book itself, paired with it because the two terms differ in wording.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r2.anchor: فعلى هذا الحكمة: هي نفس الكتاب، وجمع بينهما لاختلاف اللفظين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r3.claim: Mujāhid glosses wisdom as understanding the Qurʾan, in line with the lexical sense of comprehending meanings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r3.anchor: والحكمة في اللغة: فهم المعاني، وبه قال مجاهد، فإنه قال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim defines wisdom as knowledge joined to action; a person is not called wise unless both are present.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسلم: هي العلم والعمل، ولا يسمى الرجل حكيما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r5.speaker: ابن دريد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r5.claim: Ibn Durayd calls any saying that admonishes, rebukes, urges virtue, or restrains wrongdoing wisdom.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r5.anchor: سمعت ابن دريد يقول: كل كلمة وعظتك أو زجرتك أو دعتك إلى مكرمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r6.claim: A Prophetic saying states that some poetry contains wisdom.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r6.anchor: ومنه قوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r7.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r7.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī traces the word to restraint: a judge restrains a person from injustice, and a bridle restrains an animal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p324/r7.anchor: قال الأصمعي: أصل الحكومة: رد الرجل عن الظلم، ومنه سميت حكمة اللجام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r1.claim: Tazkiya linguistically attributes growth in untainted good deeds; zakāt means increase.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r1.anchor: أصل التزكية في اللغة: النسبة إلى الازدياد من الأفعال الحسنة التي ليست بمشوبة، والزكاة: الزيادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the phrase as guiding them to the best of worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ويرشدهم إلى أفضل عبادتك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it means purifying them from associationism and freeing them from it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جريج (¬2): يطهرهم من الشرك، ويخلصهم منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r4.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that the messenger collects the alms due on their wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r4.anchor: وقيل: يأخذ زكاة أموالهم (¬4)، وقال ابن كيسان:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r5.speaker: ابن كيسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r5.claim: Ibn Kaysān says the messenger will testify for them as just on Judgment Day because they testify that the prophets conveyed their messages.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r5.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: يشهد لهم يوم القيامة بالعدالة إذا شهدوا للأنبياء بالبلاغ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق والمفضل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r6.claim: Abū Isḥāq and al-Mufaḍḍal gloss al-ʿAzīz as the One who is inaccessible and cannot be overcome; this derives from strength, though God is not described by physical severity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r6.anchor: فقال أبو إسحاق: العزيز في صفات الله: الممتنع فلا يغلبه شيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r7.claim: The author allows divine ʿizza as invulnerability and transcendence beyond reach, but rejects describing God simply as severe or physically strong.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r7.anchor: ولا يجوز في وصف الله تعالى الشدة (¬7)، ويجوز العزة، وهي امتناعه على من أراده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو الشيباني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r8.claim: Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī’s verse uses taʿazzaza for flesh becoming firm and strong as a camel grows lean, evidencing the root sense of strength.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r8.anchor: وأنشد أبو عمرو الشيباني (¬1): أجد إذا ضمرت تعزز لحمها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r9.speaker: أبو كبير الهذلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r9.claim: Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī calls a powerful bird of prey ʿazīza; the author also cites azāz for hard ground as evidence of the root’s sense of severity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r9.anchor: وقال أبو كبير الهذلي (¬3) يصف عقابا (¬4): حتى انتهيت إلى فراش عزيزة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says al-ʿAzīz is the One whose like cannot be found.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: العزيز: الذي لا يوجد مثله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r11.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ derives al-ʿAzīz from ʿazza yaʿizzu, to be so rare that it is scarcely found.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r11.anchor: قال الفراء: يقال: عز يعز بالكسر: إذا قل حتى لا يكاد يوجد، عزة فهو عزيز

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r12.speaker: الكسائي وابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r12.claim: Al-Kisāʾī, Ibn al-Anbārī, and other linguists define al-ʿAzīz as powerful and dominant, citing the Arabic verb for overcoming and 38:23.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p325/r12.anchor: وقال الكسائي (¬6) وابن الأنباري (¬7) وجماعة من أهل اللغة: العزيز: القوي الغالب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r4.claim: The people among whom the messenger is sent are the Muslim community, and the messenger is Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r4.anchor: يريد: محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r5.claim: The Book and wisdom here mean the Quran, which the messenger recites and teaches.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r6.claim: Purifying them means cleansing them of associating partners with God.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r7.claim: Al-ʿAzīz means the prevailing, powerful one whom nothing can defeat; the meaning of al-Ḥakīm was explained earlier.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:128-130/r7.anchor: الغالب القوي الذي لا يعجزه شيء، ومضى تفسير الحكيم

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r15.claim: All exegetes understand Abraham’s prayer for a messenger from his descendants to refer especially to Muhammad’s prophethood.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r15.anchor: Hz. İbrâhim’in son duası, yüce Allah’ın kendi soyundan bir elçi göndermesini dilemesi olmuş ve bütün müfessirlerin görüşüne göre bununla da özellikle Hz. Muhammed’in risâleti kastedilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r16.claim: Ishmael settled in Mecca, lived among Jurhumites from Yemen, learned Arabic, had twelve children, and his descendants mingled with Jurhum and became Arabized as the Mustaʿriba.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r16.anchor: İsmâil aleyhisselâm Mekke’ye yerleşerek Yemen’den gelen ve Arab-ı âribe’den olan Cürhümlüler arasında yaşamış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r17.claim: Adnan, the Prophet’s twenty-first ancestor, was descended from Ishmael and thus belonged to the Arabized Mustaʿriba.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r17.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in yirmi birinci göbekten atası olan Adnan da Hz. İsmâil’in soyundan ve dolayısıyla Arab-ı müsta‘ribe’dendir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r18.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r18.claim: A hadith recorded by nearly all exegetes has Muhammad say that he is the prayer of his forefather Abraham and the glad tidings of Jesus.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r18.anchor: Hz. Peygamber, “Ben atam İbrâhim’in duası, Îsâ’nın müjdesiyim” buyurmuşlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r19.claim: The hadith’s reference to Abraham’s prayer is this verse, while Jesus’s glad tidings refers to the Saf verse saying he announced a messenger named Ahmad.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r19.anchor: İbrâhim’in duasından maksat konumuz olan 129. âyet, Îsâ’nın müjdesinden maksat da Hz. Îsâ’nın İsrâiloğulları’na hitaben

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r20.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r20.claim: Muslims made honoring Abraham alongside Muhammad in the Allahumma salli and Allahumma barik prayers a religious tradition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r20.anchor: müslümanlar, “Allâhümme salli” ve “Allâhümme bârik” dualarında, Hz. Peygamber’le birlikte Hz. İbrâhim’i de saygıyla anmayı dinî bir gelenek haline getirmişler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r21.claim: Hadiths and other Islamic sources call Abraham Khalilullah, God’s friend.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r21.anchor: hadislerde ve diğer İslâmî kaynaklarda İbrâhim aleyhisselâm Halîlullah (Allah’ın dostu) olarak isimlendirilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r22.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r22.claim: The commentary points to Muslim scholars’ arguments that the Paraclete promised in John’s Gospel is Muhammad and to announcements of the Islamic prophet in earlier scriptures.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r22.anchor: Yuhanna İncili’nde Hz. Îsâ’dan sonra geleceği bildirilen Paraklêtos’la Hz. Muhammed’in kastedildiğine dair görüşleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r23.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r23.claim: The listed tasks are highlighted as the basic functions of prophethood in messengership and guidance, though prophets have many other duties.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r23.anchor: bir peygamberin daha birçok görevi varsa da burada anılanlar, elçilik ve rehberlikle ilgili temel işlevler olması bakımından özellikle kayda değer görülmüştür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r24.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r24.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r24.claim: Exegetes explain the signs as revelation and as proofs of God’s existence and oneness and the truthfulness of prophets.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r24.anchor: Müfessirler buradaki “âyetler”i kısaca “vahiy, Allah’ın varlığını, birliğini ve peygamberlerin doğruluğunu kanıtlayan deliller”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r25.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r25.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r25.claim: Exegetes identify “the Book” as the Qur’an.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r26.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r26.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r26.claim: Exegetes explain wisdom as the Prophet’s sunnah, knowledge of religion and its rulings, and truthfulness in speech and conduct.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r26.anchor: “hikmet”i “Peygamber’in sünneti, din ve dinî hükümlerle ilgili bilgiler, söz ve yaşayışta doğruluk”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r27.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r27.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r27.claim: Exegetes understand purification as cleansing people of unbelief, polytheism, bad character, and the stain of sins.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:127/r27.anchor: “tezkiye”yi de “temizleme yani inkâr ve şirkle kötü huylardan ve günah kirlerinden arındırma”

NAHHAS:v1p262/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p262/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p262/r9.claim: «يتلو» is accusative as an adjective modifying «رسولا»; outside Qurʾānic recitation it could be jussive as the response to the prayer.
NAHHAS:v1p262/r9.anchor: يتلو في موضع نصب لأنه نعت لرسول أي رسولا تاليا ويجوز في غير القرآن جزمه

NAHHAS:v1p262/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p262/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p262/r10.claim: «ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة ويزكيهم» is coordinated to «يتلو».
NAHHAS:v1p262/r10.anchor: ( ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة ويزكيهم ) عطف عليه

BURHAN:v1p120/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p120/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p120/r1.claim: The order “teach them, then purify them” is delayed in al-Baqara, while other passages put purification first.
BURHAN:v1p120/r1.anchor: ومنه فى البقرة ﴿ يتلو عليهم آياتك ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة ويزكيهم ﴾ مؤخر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r1.claim: Baʿth and sending are close in meaning; baʿth can also mean reviving or stirring something up.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r1.anchor: البعث والارسال يتقاربان . تقول : بعثت رسولا ، وأرسلت رسولا . ويقال : البعث ، ويراد به : الإحياء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r2.claim: The verb can mean rousing a resting animal, as in stirring a she-camel.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r2.anchor: ويقال ، ويراد به : الإثارة . يقال : بعثت الناقة إذا أثرتها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r3.claim: The Day of Buʿāth was a battle day of the Aws and Khazraj.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r3.anchor: ويوم بعاث : يوم كان للأوس والخزرج

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r8.claim: Baʿth can mean sending a messenger, as in Abraham’s prayer and the mission among the unlettered.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p204/r8.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن البعث في القرآن على ستة أوجه : -

BURHAN:v1p88#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p88#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p88#2/r1.claim: The paired ending suits the verse: commissioning a messenger requires an overpowering sender, and teaching wisdom rests on the sender's wisdom.
BURHAN:v1p88#2/r1.anchor: وتعليم الرسول الحكمة لقومه إنما يكون مستندا إلى حكمة مرسله لأن الرسول واسطة بين المرسل والمرسل إليه فلا بد وأن يكون حكيما

ITQAN:v4p384/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p384/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p384/r6.claim: The requested messenger among Abraham’s descendants is Muhammad.
ITQAN:v4p384/r6.anchor: هو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v3p38/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p38/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p38/r4.claim: Causal sequence can explain divine names: might precedes judgment because power enables rule, and knowledge precedes precision; in the legal context of al-Anʿam, wisdom precedes knowledge.
ITQAN:v3p38/r4.anchor: السابع السببية كتقديم العزيز على الحكيم لأنه عز فحكم والعليم عليه لأن الإحكام والإتقان ناشئ عن العلم

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r3.claim: Ibn Jinni defends the reading with a still mīm, arguing Sibawayh accurately transmitted what he heard and that Abu al-ʿAbbās’s alternative cannot fit the poetic meter.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p15#6/r3.anchor: كما في الاحتجاج لقراءة: "ويعلمهم الكتاب"1 بسكون الميم
